item.title: 'The Body' Ending Explained: Is Grace Possessed? Netflix Showrunners Talk Season 2
item.description: The Body , Netflix’s new campy-horror TV series , came out this week. But based on a quick social media browse, it might as well have come out months ago. item.title: Portugal redesigns No. 7 shirt to honour Ronaldo after retirement
item.description: By Ayobami Okerinde Portugal have announced a redesign of the No. 7 on their national team shirts in tribute to former captain Cristiano Ronaldo following his retirement from international football. The Portuguese Football Federation (FPF) announced the change on Saturday, saying the new design would preserve the legacy of the number associated with the 41-year-old forward. In a statement shared by football transfer expert Fabrizio Romano, the federation said the decision was another way to immortalise the significance of the number and honour Ronaldo’s contribution to Portuguese football. “This is another way to eternalise the meaning of such a special number and honour the legacy it represents for us. “Because there are stories, memories, all the achievements and emotions, which will forever be linked to Cristiano Ronaldo. “From today we will thus have a different number 7 on the sweater, with the same essence and the same pride, reserving the previous one for the eternalisation of the story that will never be forgotten. Thank you, Cristiano!” the statement read. Ronaldo announced his retirement from the Portugal national team on November 5, bringing an end to his 23-year international career. In a message to Portuguese supporters, the forward said it was time to hand back the national team shirt and captain’s armband after enjoying the privilege of representing his country for more than two decades. “For 23 years, I had the privilege and responsibility of wearing it, defending it, and carrying it with me to stadiums all around the world,” he said. Ronaldo finished his international career as Portugal’s record appearance-maker, with 234 caps, and all-time leading scorer, with 146 goals. He also captained the country to its first European Championship title in 2016 and two UEFA Nations League triumphs in 2019 and 2025. The post Portugal redesigns No. 7 shirt to honour Ronaldo after retirement appeared first on Vanguard News .

item.title: Yilwatda charges North-Central APC leaders to unite for Tinubu
item.description: The National Chairman of the All Progressives Congress (APC), Prof. Nentawe Yilwatda, has charged governors, governorship candidates and party leaders across the North-Central region to unite stakeholders and intensify mobilisation for President Bola Tinubu’s re-election in the January 16, 2027 presidential election. Yilwatda gave the charge at the APC presidential campaign rally held at Azaria Road Stadium, Jos, Plateau State, where Tinubu’s campaign train received a large turnout of party leaders, supporters and residents. The APC national chairman expressed satisfaction with the turnout and what he described as a renewed spirit of unity among party leaders and supporters in Plateau State. He urged residents to translate the enthusiasm demonstrated at the rally into votes, insisting that the state must deliver a record-breaking victory for Tinubu. Yilwatda declared that political leaders in Plateau State were fully united behind the President, assuring him that the support demonstrated at the rally would be reflected at the ballot box. He also described Tinubu as a promise keeper who had fulfilled his commitments to Plateau State, saying the administration’s performance provided a basis for continued public support. A major highlight of the rally was the presentation of APC flags to the party’s governorship candidates across the North-Central states, in what the party described as a demonstration of its commitment to strengthening its political structures and securing victory at all levels. Speaking further, Yilwatda urged APC governors, governorship candidates and party leaders in the region to set aside personal interests and political differences, unite all stakeholders and work towards a common electoral objective. In Plateau State, he urged party leaders to consolidate the unity already achieved and mobilise support for Tinubu and all APC candidates. In Benue State, he called on the governor and party leaders to harmonise competing interests, bring political stakeholders together and mobilise voters for the party. For Niger State, the APC chairman expressed confidence in the state leadership’s ability to use the party’s flag as a rallying point to unite members and secure victory for Tinubu and other candidates. Similarly, while presenting the party’s flag to its governorship candidate in Nasarawa State, Wadada, Yilwatda urged him and other party leaders to provide purposeful leadership, unite stakeholders and mobilise support for the President. He also called for concerted efforts towards greater prosperity, peace and development in the state. The APC chairman stressed that the North-Central region must approach the 2027 elections with a common purpose, urging party structures, elected officials, candidates and grassroots mobilisers to intensify engagement with voters. He said the enthusiasm witnessed at the Jos rally must be sustained and translated into votes across the region. “Our strength lies in our unity, our strategy is effective

item.title: Table tennis: BVB back to winning ways
item.description: Table tennis: BVB back to winning ways Team news Fadeev skilfully used his players’ disappointment at the sobering result in Bremen as motivation for the clash with the 2025 double winners. With star player Anders Lind and former doubles world champion Kristian Karlsson both sidelined through injury, the 51-year-old once again put his faith in summer signings Wim Verdonschot at number one and Joao Geraldo at number three. The coach made just one change, at number two: Adam Szudi replaced Cedric Nuytinck. The Hungarian, one of last season’s surprise performers, thus made his first appearance of the season. How the match unfolded The 600 spectators witnessed a match full of twists and turns in all three singles contests, making for a particularly thrilling encounter. In the opening singles, young international Verdonschot needed a deciding game to beat Tiago Abiodun despite twice taking the lead, as did Szudi against Ochsenhausen’s doubles world champion Shunsuke Togami in the next match. Geraldo also saw Iulian Chirita draw level at 1-1 before securing a four-game victory. Adam Szudi was undoubtedly the celebrated “Man of the Match” as BVB claimed their third consecutive win over Ochsenhausen. The 30-year-old repeatedly caught Togami, ranked 15th in the world, off guard. Szudi, primarily a doubles specialist who made his mark last season with eight wins in 18 singles matches, coped surprisingly well with his Japanese opponent’s powerful play and frequently took the initiative himself. All too often, Togami had no answer. Szudi was understandably delighted after his upset win: “You don’t beat a reigning world champion every day.” The right-hander’s surprise victory played a key role in Dortmund’s third-most emphatic Bundesliga win. BVB have conceded fewer than five games in a 3-0 victory on only two occasions: in November 2024 during their debut season against TTC OE Bad Homburg (four games), and just over three months ago this season against ASC Grünwettersbach (one game). Reaction Ursula Reitemeyer (Head of Table Tennis): “Our boys gave 110 per cent. Adam’s win against Togami was sensational. With our fans acting as our ‘twelfth man’, the team more than made up for the defeat against Bremen. We’ll keep pushing.” Evgeny Fadeev (Coach): “What a response after the 3-0 defeat in Bremen! A superb performance from everyone, a real team victory. Afterwards in the dressing room, we were asking ourselves how we could look like a completely different team just 48 hours after Bremen. But our in-depth discussions about the Bremen match and the lessons we learned from that defeat clearly paid off. That gave me a really good feeling going into this match, and absolutely everyone stayed focused right to the end. Adam’s win against Togami provided the decisive turning point, because it really was a breakthrough, a point against a world champion that none of us could have expected – and in his first match of the season. But I’m also really pleased for Wim and Joa

item.title: Bears Must Lock Up Theo Benedet And Jonah Jackson Now
item.description: Mike Dinovo-Imagn Images Since Caleb Williams remains on a cheap rookie deal, the front office has room to spend big on the players who actually make the team win. The logic behind each move is sound as Sports Illustrated reports that four Bears secured contract extensions for 2027 and beyond. The team has proven it can find value, and now it must pay for it before the market does. The most urgent case involves Theo Benedet. After losing the starting left tackle competition at camp, he assumed the position when Braxton Jones suffered a season-ending injury. He did not panic. Benedet has allowed only one sack and 18 pressures while maintaining a pass-blocking grade of 68.4 through nine games, according to reports. In the run game, he ranks 19th among tackles in the NFL with a 73.3 grade. Waiting is a poor strategy even though the Bears hold complete authority over him once he becomes an exclusive rights free agent following this season. A player who holds the line this well deserves a long-term deal as a potential swing tackle or starter. Jackson’s Turnaround Demands Cash Then there is Jonah Jackson, a story of redemption that the Bears must finish. After the team acquired him in a 2025 trade with the Rams, his career appeared finished because he missed most of that season due to injury. This season has been particularly impressive, with Jackson ranking fourth in run-blocking grade at 85.1 and fifth in overall grade at 83.1 among guards while not permitting a sack. Although he is under contract for another year, he has no guaranteed money left on his deal. That makes him a perfect candidate for a long-term extension. Locking him up now also lowers his $12.2 million cap hit for 2027. Future Plans for D’Marco Jackson The report also highlights linebacker D’Marco Jackson, who started his ascension last season as a pleasant surprise for Chicago. He is another player whose play has earned him a spot on the extension list. The team has the flexibility to keep these core pieces together while Caleb Williams matures. The Bears are 7-2 and sitting in first place in the NFC North, so keeping the offensive line solid is the smartest play they can make. Sports Illustrated reports that the team may allocate resources to players who have demonstrated their value while in Chicago. With a strong 7-2 record marking the midway point of the 2026 season, the Bears have landed their bye in an ideal spot to take stock of these performances.

item.title: Michigan football vs Oregon game day injuries: OT Blake Frazier is out
item.description: Michigan football will have a new offensive line configuration on the West Coast. U-M (5-4, 2-4 Big Ten) will be without offensive tackle Blake Frazier in the Week 11 contest against Oregon (6-3, 4-2 Big Ten). He left last week's loss to MSU in the second half and was officially ruled out in the pregame availability report provided to the Big Ten two hours before kickoff (3:30 p.m., FS1). The Wolverines could also be without right guard Brady Norton, who got banged up a week ago as well and played just 26 snaps. Norton, who's listed as a game-time decision, missed Michigan's Week 7 win over Penn State but has been a consistent part of the rotation, playing 446 snaps (the fourth most of any offensive lineman on the team) this year. Elsewhere, Michigan is down a rotational wide receiver in Channing Goodwin. The junior wideout only has two grabs for 32 yards this season but is frequently on the field, having played the third-most snaps (127) of any wideout, though Salesi Moa and Travis Johnson has been earning more playing time of late. Tight ends Hogan Hansen and Jalen Hoffman, who were listed as questionable all week, were both removed from the report. Hansen missed the first two games of the season and then was banged up last week, playing just six snaps. Hoffman hasn't missed any time yet this season. MICHIGAN VS OREGON PREDICTION: Will OC change make a difference? U-M got good news on the defensive side of the ball. Edge rushers John Henry Daley and Dom Nichols and safety Rod Moore were all listed as questionable but have been removed from the report, indicating all are good to go. The only player missing (who hasn't been out the whole year) on the defensive side of the ball is edge Nate Marshall, who was suspended indefinitely earlier this week. Tony Garcia is the Michigan beat writer for the Detroit Free Press. Email him at apgarcia@freepress.com and follow him on X at @RealTonyGarcia . item.title: Ella Swindle to leave Texas volleyball; Jerritt Elliot emotional about setter's departure
item.description: Texas Longhorns setter Ella Swindle (1) celebrates a score during the NCAA Regional Final volleyball match against Wisconsin at Gregory Gym on Sunday, Dec. 14, 2025 in Austin. (Aaron E. Martinez/Austin American-Statesman) Ella Swindle could have up to 10 more games in a Texas volleyball uniform, but Friday's sweep of Ole Miss served as a farewell of sorts for the star-crossed setter, who won't play for the Longhorns in her fifth and final collegiate season in 2027. After an emotional postgame senior night celebration that included rounds of hugs and even more tears, Swindle confirmed to reporters after the match that she plans to leave Texas (14-8, 10-4 SEC) following this year, which continues Sunday against LSU in the regular-season finale. The Texas Longhorns celebrate beating Texas A&M in the Lone Star Showdown volleyball match at Gregory Gym on Sunday, Nov. 1, 2026 in Austin. (Aaron E. Martinez/Austin American-Statesman) "I'm definitely not done with volleyball," she said. "I'm kind of figuring things out. I think I'll know for sure in the next week or so. But I'm just praying about it a lot, and I know there's a really great plan in store. I've just been where my feet are and focusing on the moment that I'm in, but I'm definitely getting excited for what's next." Swindle's departure comes as no surprise, especially after fellow 2023 recruiting class members Torrey Stafford , Nya Bunton and Ramsey Gary announced their decision earlier this week to return to Texas for the 2027 season. Swindle and defensive specialist Anja Kujundžić were not a part of that announcement even though both four-year players still have one remaining year of eligibility. Both partook in Friday's senior night celebration. Setter in and out of rotation since freshman season By now, most Longhorn fans understand Swindle's saga. She helped lead Texas to a second consecutive national championship while earning freshman All-American honors in 2023, when she started all 32 matches and playing in all 114 sets. During her lone season as the full-time setter, Swindle amassed 1,088 assists, 227 digs and 92 blocks. But that season proved a high mark for Swindle at Texas. She served as the second setter to Averi Carlson as a sophomore before regaining the starting job last season. This year, she fell behind starter Rella Binney and freshman Genevieve Harris in the rotation and has only appeared in 10 matches. Prior to an emotional homecoming in the Longhorns' win Nov. 6 in Swindle's hometown of Columbia, Mo., Swindle had gone more than a month without seeing the court. Texas coach Jerritt Elliott has treaded lightly over the past few seasons when discussing his decisions at the setter position. But the coach has relied on advanced metrics throughout his 26 seasons leading the Longhorns, and the numbers showed that the offense clicked at a higher rate when setters other than Swindle directed the attack. item.title: Joseph scores record-equalling five tries as England rout Japan
item.description: Douglas Lambert, Rory Underwood, Josh Lewsey and Henry Arundell are the other players to have scored five tries in a single match for England [Getty Images] Nations Championship England (49) 78 Tries: Joseph 5, Steward, Genge, Murley, Earl, Martin, B Curry, M Smith, Fisilau Cons: Ford 4, Slade Pen: Ford Japan (10) 15 Tries: Dearns, Helu Con: Saito Pen: Saito Will Joseph marked his comeback after four years out the Test game with a record-equalling five tries as England tore through Japan and set their sights on New Zealand next weekend. A teenage Joseph made his debut as a late replacement in a game against Australia four years ago. Since then he has endured his boyhood club London Irish going bust, an underwhelming spell at Harlequins and the loss of hearing in his left ear after an auto-immune reaction. But his superb early season form for Gloucester has thrust him back into the international picture and he took his opportunity superbly, showing work-rate and intelligence as well as raw top-end speed. Four other players - Douglas Lambert, Rory Underwood, Josh Lewsey and Henry Arundell - have scored five tries in a single match for England. Japan were vastly over-matched, unable to rev up the ball movement and quickfire rucks that have made them a threat to the game's major powers in the past. With the outcome clear as England raced out to a 32-3 lead inside 20 minutes, the focus sharpened on a number of individuals attempting to press their case alongside Joseph. Centre Max Ojomoh, making his first appearance since an excellent performance against Argentina 12 months ago, was smart and sharp in midfield. The Bath man burst into a pocket of space to help set up Joseph's second and his slick hands opened up a corridor of space for his team-mate's gleefully acrobatic fourth as Japan were buried beneath an avalanche of points. Henry Pollock, afforded only his second start in his eye-catching England career, carried gamely but didn't have the impact he has shown so often off the bench. Replacement Greg Fisilau's pair of wince-inducing hits and burrowing try added more intrigue to the back-row equation. And while George Ford sewed together England's backline neatly enough, his failure to convert more of England's early tries won't help his hopes of regaining the 10 shirt on a more permanent basis. Northampton scrum-half Archie McParland made his debut as a replacement, but a host of front-line names will return next Saturday as England attempt to take down an All Blacks side smarting from defeat by Wales. Joseph fills Feyi-Waboso vacancy with aplomb England have targeted fast starts this autumn and they tore into Japan with relish, launching into a pummelling that only let up long after victory was secure. Joseph, tasked with bringing the pace and power lost with Immanuel Feyi-Waboso's injury, delivered almost immediately. item.title: Ex-CFB coach eviscerates SEC Commissioner Greg Sankey over Ole Miss-Oklahoma scheduling
item.description: Mandatory Credit: Butch Dill-Imagn Images Ex-CFB coach eviscerates SEC Commissioner Greg Sankey over Ole Miss-Oklahoma scheduling appeared first on ClutchPoints . Add ClutchPoints as a Preferred Source by clicking here . On Friday, the nationwide FAA ground-threw college football into a frenzy . As a result, schedules were all over the map. Ultimately, SEC Commissioner Greg Sankey rescheduled the Ole Miss/Oklahoma game from Saturday to Sunday. That decision drew the ire of former college football coach Bob Stoops, summed up in a post on X, formerly Twitter. He specifically cited that other games on the schedule are moving ahead as planned. “This decision by Greg Sankey is absolutely wrong,” Stoops posted. “All of the power 4 teams found a way to make it to their games, but Ole Miss wouldn’t 🤔 ASU is flying across country to UCF this AM to play today. Greg Sankey instead of telling OU they would forfeit if they didn’t change the day, he could have told Ole Miss they will forfeit if they didn’t find a way to Norman even if game is delayed. But instead he didn’t!!” Watch sports LIVE with fuboTV (free trial) This decision by Greg Sankey is absolutely wrong. All of the power 4 teams found a way to make it to their games, but Ole Miss wouldn't 🤔 ASU is flying across country to UCF this AM to play today. Greg Sankey instead of telling OU they would forfeit if they didn't change the… — Bob Stoops (@CoachBobStoops) November 14, 2026 Over 4,000 flights were delayed, and 12,500 were canceled because of the fiasco. A communications issue was cited as the cause by the FAA. As a result, college teams had to make adjustments. Purdue traveled by bus to Iowa for Saturday’s game. Altogether, the SEC has seven games scheduled for Saturday. The games are: Alabama at Vanderbilt, No. 8 Tennessee at Texas A&M, No. 22 Missouri at No. 1 Georgia, Auburn at Mississippi State, Florida at No. 11 Kentucky, No. 6 Texas at LSU, and No. 17 South Carolina at Arkansas. On Sunday, Ole Miss and Oklahoma will kick off at noon CST/1:00 pm EST in Norman, Oklahoma. item.title: 🔥 In-demand Antonio Nusa continues post-World Cup form for Norway
item.description: 🔥 In-demand Antonio Nusa continues post-World Cup form for Norway Norway's resurgence on the European stage at both the club and international level has been something brilliant for Nordic football. Though Erling Haaland will undoubtedly continue to receive the attention he so richly deserves, and much of the same can be said of captain Martin Ødegaard, the supporting cast for Ståle Solbakken's Røde, Hvite, Blå deserves plenty of praise. Antonio Nusa, perhaps, more than any other. Still just 21, the RB Leipzig starlet has been in some of the finest form of his career after a very credible summer with Norway at the 2026 World Cup. That hot streak continued this evening in Oslo when he opened the scoring in Norway's Nations League A home clash against Wales, meaning Nusa has now found the back of the net or collected an assist in six-straight matches for club and country since his brace of helpers against Elversberg back on 24 October. Taking up his position on the left flank, Nusa did well to beat veteran shot-stopper Karl Darlow with a low drive from the top of the 18-yard box to break the deadlock after the half-time interval. It was Nusa's 10th goal for Norway, and the first for his country since the pair he bagged over the summer across the Atlantic. His pace outwide, competence on the ball, and ability to drive play forward at speed have been at the forefront of Norway's rekindling efforts, and perhaps it's no wonder that Premier League holders and current table-toppers Arsenal have recently been heavily linked with the former Club Brugge standout. Having started alongside the aforementioned Haaland and Ødegaard, as well as Fulham's Oscar Bobb tonight, will Nusa add his name to Norway's Premier League-based ranks come the opening of the January window?

item.title: Is Ireland v Fiji on TV? Channel, kick-off time and how to watch Nations Championship
item.description: Ireland will continue their push for top spot in the northern hemisphere pool of the Nations Championship as they take on Fiji in Dublin. Andy Farrell’s side kicked off their November with a good win against Argentina last Friday, with an encounter with South Africa next week looming as the defining test of their autumn. They will be wary, though, of a Fiji side that showed some encouraging signs in defeat to France as they continue to bed in under new coach Jake White. The veteran South African coach will be hoping to mastermind a shock as the Pacific Islanders take on a rotated Irish team. Here’s everything you need to know. When is Ireland vs Fiji? Ireland vs Fiji is due to kick off at 8.10pm GMT on Saturday 14 November at the Aviva Stadium in Dublin. How can I watch it? Viewers in the United Kingdom can watch the match live on ITV1, with coverage from 7.30pm GMT. A live stream will be available via ITVX. Team news With Sean Jansen joining Caelan Doris and Jack Conan on the sidelines, Nick Timoney moves to the problem position of No 8 for Ireland. Josh van der Flier is a handy addition on the openside in his stead, while Tadhg Beirne takes over the captaincy from Dan Sheehan, who is working through return-to-play protocols after a concussion. Mack Hansen moves to full-back in a tweaked backline as Jamison Gibson-Park, Tommy O’Brien, Bundee Aki and Jamie Osborne all come in. Among the replacements, an Ireland debut awaits James McNabney of Ulster. Ireland XV: 1 Andrew Porter, 2 Ronan Kelleher, 3 Tadhg Furlong; 4 James Ryan, 5 Tadhg Beirne (capt.); 6 Ryan Baird, 7 Josh van der Flier, 8 Nick Timoney; 9 Jamison Gibson-Park, 10 Sam Prendergast; 11 Tommy O’Brien, 12 Bundee Aki, 13 Jamie Osborne, 14 Robert Baloucoune; 15 Mack Hansen. Replacements: 16 Tom Stewart, 17 Tom O’Toole, 18 Sam Illo, 19 Darragh Murray, 20 James McNabney; 21 Craig Casey, 22 Ciaran Frawley, 23 Stuart McCloskey. Fiji also make a number of changes as recently-installed head coach Jake White continues to explore the depth of his squad. Veteran fly half Ben Volavola is brought in to steer the ship while stalwart back rower Peceli Yato leads the side from No 8. Outside centre Setareki Bituniyata makes a 15-a-side international debut at the age of 31 having gone been named ProD2 player of the season after a standout campaign for Provence last year. Salesi Rayasi is out injured. Fiji XV: 1 Peni Ravai, 2 Tevita Ikannivere, 3 Luke Tagi; 4 Joseva Tamani, 5 Isoa Nasilasila; 6 Mesake Vocevoce, 7 Lekima Tagitagivalu, 8 Peceli Yato (capt.); 9 Frank Lomani, 10 Ben Volavola; 11 Jiuta Wainiqolo, 12 Josua Tuisova, 13 Setareki Bituniyata, 14 Selestino Ravutaumada; 15 Ponipate Loganimasi. Replacements: 16 Zuriel Togiatama, 17 Vilikesa Nairau, 18 Inoke Ravuiwasa, 19 Kitione Salawa, 20 Elia Canakaivata; 21 Terio Tamani, 22 Caleb Muntz, 23 Iosefo Masi.

item.title: Cavaliers vs. Mavericks Prediction: Preview, Injury Report, Advantages, X-Factors
item.description: Mandatory Credit: Kevin Jairaj-Imagn Images The Cleveland Cavaliers could be missing almost their entire starting lineup tonight, and that’s a huge problem with the Dallas Mavericks coming to town. Evan Mobley is already out, while Donovan Mitchell , James Harden , and Jarrett Allen are all questionable. Dallas has some injuries too, but the Cavaliers have much more to worry about before their game at the Rocket Arena on Saturday, November 14, at 7:30 p.m. ET. Cleveland is 6-7, seventh in the East with a 4-2 home record, after losing 133-121 to the Miami Heat on Friday . Mitchell leads the team with 23.0 points, 4.9 rebounds, and 5.6 assists per game, while Harden has 16.9 points, 4.7 rebounds, and 5.8 assists. Both players could miss tonight’s game, which would leave Cleveland without its two main guards. The Mavericks are 7-5, 10th in the West with a 2-3 road record, after losing 133-94 to the Minnesota Timberwolves on Thursday. Cooper Flagg has been great with 24.6 points, 6.9 rebounds, and 6.5 assists per game, while Kyrie Irving is putting up 21.6 points, 3.2 rebounds, and 4.3 assists. The teams split their two games last season, and this will be their first meeting in 2026-27. Injury Report Cavaliers Jarrett Allen: Questionable (right knee injury management) James Harden: Questionable (left lower leg/calf tightness) Donovan Mitchell: Questionable (left knee contusion/injury management) Peyton Watson: Questionable (right hamstring injury management) Sam Merrill: Out (right elbow injury management) Evan Mobley: Out (left great toe sprain) Nae’Qwan Tomlin: Out (low back stress reaction) Ernest Udeh Jr.: Out (G League two-way) Mavericks Caleb Martin: Available (right thumb splint) Morez Johnson Jr.: Probable (left shin/tibia contusion) Max Christie: Doubtful (left ankle sprain) Tarik Biberovic: Out (right heel bursitis) Sergio de Larrea: Out (right knee sprain) Dereck Lively II: Out (right foot surgery) Why The Cavaliers Have The Advantage Cleveland has been scoring more points than Dallas this season, and that’s one of the few advantages the Cavaliers have tonight. They’re putting up 116.8 points per game, eighth in the NBA, while the Mavericks are scoring 113.2, ranking 17th. Cleveland also has a 117.0 offensive rating, 10th in the league, compared to Dallas’ 113.7, which ranks 17th. The Cavaliers are also shooting much better from outside. They’re making 37.0% of their threes, eighth in the NBA, while Dallas is shooting only 33.6%, ranking 21st. Mitchell is making 38.1% of his threes, Harden is at 37.4%, and Meleek Thomas has been excellent at 47.3%. Cleveland has enough good shooters to cause some problems, but that depends a lot on Mitchell and Harden being available. And those two guards are the biggest reason Cleveland still has a chance. Mitchell already scored 37 points against the New York Knicks on November 7, while Harden has been getting almost six assists per game. item.title: Jets vs. Bills: 3 key matchups to watch in Week 10
item.description: The New York Jets (2-7) will look to snap a four game losing streak in Week 10 when they host the Buffalo Bills at MetLife Stadium. The Jets suffered a brutal 35-12 loss to the Kansas City Chiefs at Arrowhead Stadium. Buffalo (7-1) will be looking for their fifth-straight win after defeating the Minnesota Vikings 23-6 last week. Here are Jets Wire's three key matchups for the team's Week 10 matchup vs. the Buffalo Bills: Will McDonald vs. Aaron Glenn There was a lot of drama surrounding defensive end Will McDonald during the trade deadline. Reports surfaced that an AFC team made a "significant offer" to the Jets for the former first-round pick, but it was turned down. As more information was revealed, the significant offer was reportedly a Day 2 pick, which enraged Jets nation on social media. There was another report stating that McDonald asked for a trade saying he was unhappy with his playing time, which only added to the confusion as to why they would keep a player on their roster that wanted out. But, Glenn and Mougey decided to keep McDonald with the head coach telling reporters earlier this week that he had earned a larger role on defense and will see extended playing time beginning with Sunday's game against the Bills. McDonald has been rather unimpressive in his fourth season with the Jets as he only has three sacks in nine games. While he still grades out well as a pass rusher, he still struggles against the run, which is an area the Jets were hoping to see more improvement. We'll see if Glenn is a man of his word when it comes to McDonald's playing time on Sunday. If he does indeed see an increased role on the defense, then it's up to the former first-round pick to make the most of it. David Bailey vs. Spencer Brown / Tylan Grable Bailey was an absolute beast last week and the lone bright spot in the Jets loss to Kansas City. The rookie had 2 sacks and 2 forced fumbles on the same drive! Bailey now has 7.5 sacks on the season, which puts him tied for fourth in the league and he has five forced fumbles, which puts him tied for first. Buffalo's starting right tackle Spencer Brown is listed as doubtful with an ankle injury and if he can't play, than Grable will step in for his second start of the season. He's a third year player from Central Florida who was selected in the sixth round of the 2024 draft. He stepped in last week for the injured Dion Dawkins and performed well, but committed a few penalties. item.title: 'I was envious': R Ashwin makes honest confession about Ravindra Jadeja
item.description: Ravichandran Ashwin has offered an interesting account of what made his bowling partnership with Ravindra Jadeja so successful, revealing how he learned to use the left-arm spinner's strengths and limitations to his advantage. Ashwin described Jadeja as an exceptionally gifted cricketer but suggested that the all-rounder initially lacked the instinct to consistently find ways to dismiss batters. The two formed one of the most successful spin combinations in Test cricket, sharing the field in 58 matches and accounting for 587 wickets. While Ashwin claimed 317 of those dismissals, Jadeja contributed 270. According to the former India off-spinner, their success stemmed from understanding each other's contrasting approaches and making the most of them. Speaking on Aakash Chopra's podcast show, Baith & Bol, Ashwin explained that he understood Jadeja's game well enough to help him operate within his strengths rather than push him towards something that did not come naturally to him. “I know his limitations well," Ashwin said. “Very few can bring him out of those limitations. I was one of them. His biggest strength: naturally gifted. If he has a bad day, you just tell him your effort is fine; tomorrow will be better. His action was simple, release point simple, tappa so good—he doesn’t have to think. He didn’t know how to dismiss batsmen—I’m saying he absolutely didn’t know. But his skill to choke batsmen was intertwined with his skill. You can’t sweep him—trajectory is low. You can’t step out—airspeed is good. You can’t play defense without doubting if the ball would remain the same." One aspect of Jadeja's bowling that often came under scrutiny was his reluctance to vary his pace or give the ball more flight, even when the conditions called for it. Ashwin revealed that he had attempted to persuade his spin partner to experiment more, but those efforts often came at the expense of Jadeja's effectiveness and economy. Eventually, Ashwin recognised that Jadeja's ability to keep things tight from one end gave him the freedom to attack from the other. While Jadeja restricted the opposition's scoring opportunities, Ashwin could experiment with different deliveries and concentrate on taking wickets. That combination also made Jadeja more difficult to deal with. Ashwin said developing this understanding gave him even greater appreciation for what Jadeja brought to the team, particularly his remarkable consistency and control. “When I understood that, my respect for Jadeja doubled—what he does is not easy. I have seen many skillful spinners, but the repetitive nature- keeping the ball there at the same speed is very difficult. Spinning the ball at that speed is not easy," he said. Ashwin also spoke candidly about experiencing a sense of envy towards Jadeja's natural abilities, although he clarified that he was never jealous of his teammate's success. item.title: 'We've waited 73 years to be here' - Wales fans ecstatic after win over New Zealand
item.description: Saturday marked the first time Wales had beaten New Zealand in 73 years [Getty Images] Welsh rugby fans were "fizzing off their heads" on Saturday night after ending 73 years of hurt against New Zealand in an epic Nations Championship encounter. The match at the Principality Stadium ended 35-28 to the hosts as the All Blacks' run of 34 successive victories against Wales - dating back to 1953 - came to a juddering halt in Cardiff. Wales fans were left stunned by a result that came just a week on from having to grind out a win against Japan. Celebrities were also quick to congratulate the team with Gavin & Stacey star Ruth Jones sharing her disbelief in an Instagram post. Three times Wales led by 14 points, and for the first time in history they scored five tries against New Zealand, but ultimately it was heroic defensive work that denied the visitors. All Blacks head coach Dave Rennie made eight changes from the side that swept past Scotland in their previous Nations Championship game. But the approach backfired spectacularly after a brilliant performance sparked astonishing scenes in Cardiff. Darren Williams went to Caernarfon Rugby Club to watch the match [BBC] Darren Williams lives abroad but comes home once a year to visit his family in Wales. He came to Caernarfon Rugby Club to watch the match and said the result was "excellent". "I hope they can continue like this and keep moving forward," he said. "The atmosphere was excellent and very enthusiastic." Daron Owens said she was "really glad" to be at the rugby club to witness such a brilliant performance. "It was great to see everyone so proud. Everyone was cheering so loudly, it was a really positive place to be." One fan pitch side at Principality Stadium said they had waited "73 years to be at this game", adding that they were in "total shock but absolutely delighted". Daron Owens said everyone at the rugby club was "ecstatic" after the game [BBC] Celebrities and politicians were also quick to pay tribute to the team for their heroics on the field. Gavin and Stacey star Jones shared her sheer delight in an Instagram video, with the actor looked visibly stunned following the incredible win over New Zealand. Welsh politicians have also come forward to congratulate the team, including First Minister Rhun ap Iorwerth. "This has been decades in the making. Huge congratulations to you all," he wrote on Facebook. "You should all be proud." Secretary of State for Wales Stephen Kinnock said he managed to watch the final part of the game after speaking at the Welsh Labour conference in Llandudno. "After 73 years we've finally beaten the All Blacks! Can barely believe what I've just witnessed," he said. item.title: Brewers Reportedly Unlikely To Pursure This Star Free Agent To Replace Jake Bauers
item.description: Boston Red Sox designated hitter Jake Bauers The Milwaukee Brewers are losing Jake Bauers to the Boston Red Sox, but fans should not expect them to make a big splash to replace him. Ty France had his best season since his 2022 All-Star campaign, and he is also on the open market. Production-wise, he would be a great replacement for Bauers. However, the Brewers' chances of pursuing him are slim, per The Athletic's Will Sammon and Ken Rosenthal. "The chances of the Brewers pursuing free agent Ty France, a right-handed hitter who like Bauers enjoyed a breakout season in 2026, would appear slim," wrote The Athletic. "France, 32, is a year older than Bauers and figures to command a strong multiyear deal of his own." The reality is, France is going to be out of the Brewers' price range most likely, and they already have in-house options to replace Bauers. For one, they have Andrew Vaughn, who would have been the starting first baseman anyway if not for an injury that gave Bauers a shot to play regularly. As far as a left-handed option at first base, the Brewers have Blake Burke and Andrew Fischer in the minor leagues, knocking on the door of the big leagues. Fischer is only in Double-A, but he hit 48 home runs last season. The Brewers don't really need a platoon bat to pair with Vaughn either. He can handle lefties and righties. He crushed lefties last year, but in 198 plate appearances against righties, he slashed .285/.369/.395. He had a .764 OPS against right-handed pitching. item.title: Wales believed they could create history - Lake
item.description: Dewi Lake and Jac Morgan were the Wales co-captains at the 2023 World Cup in France [Huw Evans Picture Agency] Captain Dewi Lake says he always believed Wales could defeat New Zealand and end the 73-year hoodoo against the All Blacks. Wales never trailed in the 35-28 victory as they produced a magnificent display to beat New Zealand for the first time since 1953. Wales had lost the previous 34 matches in the fixture and had odds of 20-1 with the bookmakers before this game. But Lake says the group thought they could win against a New Zealand team ranked second in the world and would have gone top if they had beaten Wales. "Of course we did," said Lake. "Sometimes we sit in front of the media and say we can beat them and it's probably a passing comment for some media outlets or people at home. "It's not for us. We work hard, we have tough conversations, not only players, but coaches and staff. "There is much hard work that goes on for this group to grow and succeed. "For it to finally come to fruition and see it on the field makes me so proud." This is a special group - Tandy Lake's sentiments were echoed by head coach Tandy, who said he felt emotional after the win. "You could see what it means for the the players, nation and supporters," said Tandy. "It's incredible. We've been wanting some positivity and the players delivered that. "The overriding emotion is pride for the playing group, the staff and I'm just glad for everyone who represents Wales. "You always have belief. History tells you something different but I believe in the group. "They are a special group of people and I can't wait to come in every Monday to work with them." Nations Championship: Wales end 73-year wait to beat New Zealand - reaction Magnificent Wales end 73-year New Zealand hoodoo All Blacks ran into a Welsh brick wall - Barrett Lake's half-time team talk galvanises Wales Wales led 14-0 and 21-7 in the first half before the All Blacks levelled the score at half-time. That is when New Zealand have traditionally gone away to secure victory, as they did 12 months ago in a 52-26 success, but there was no repeat this time. "I did love it at half-time with the playing group, listening to them talk to each other," said Tandy. "The way the skipper spoken about around what's coming from the next 40 minutes was outstanding." Lake added: "I won't tell you exactly what I said because I think that's a privilege that the group that we're in the room should keep. "But it was more or less a flashback to 12 months ago when we were in a similar position at half-time. "We were not quite in the lead or drawing, but there or thereabouts and it was just a reminder of that feeling for us." Dynamic defence sees Wales home Wales responded with two more tries before New Zealand brought back the deficit to within seven points. What followed was a defensive effort rarely seen by Wales in recent years with Gareth Thomas, James Botham, Jac Morgan and Dan Edwards involved in holding up New Zealand ov

item.title: All Blacks ran into a Welsh brick wall - Barrett
item.description: Beauden Barrett won his 149th New Zealand cap against Wales [Press Association] Beauden Barrett said it felt like New Zealand were running into a red brick wall after they became the first All Blacks side to lose to Wales since 1953. Steve Tandy's men created history with a 35-28 victory at Principality Stadium thanks to a stirring defensive effort. Wales scored five tries - a national record against New Zealand - but it was their effort without the ball that ended a 34-game losing streak against the All Blacks. The home side made 346 tackles, with lock Dafydd Jenkins topping the chart with 38, and held the New Zealanders up over the line three times in the second half to protect their seven-point lead. "It felt like a brick wall at times, so you have to give them credit," said full-back Barrett, who captained New Zealand in a Test for the first time. "You give opportunities for the crowd to come into the game, and we are well aware of that when we come here. "That's why it's one of the best places to play rugby - it feels like you are playing 16 or 17." Magnificent Wales end 73-year New Zealand hoodoo Wales believed they could create history - Lake As it happened: Wales claim first win over New Zealand since 1953 Dave Rennie claimed an unwanted piece of history as the first All Blacks coach to lose to Wales in 73 years. The former Glasgow boss admitted New Zealand "certainly got out-passioned" but had no regrets about his selection. The All Blacks made eight changes to their starting line-up between their win against Scotland and their trip to England in the final Nations Championship group game. "We had a good enough side on the field to win, and if you look at the stats, we had plenty of opportunities and the guys created a lot of chances," said Rennie. "We just weren't clinical enough, and they were very good defensively. "I have no regret around the side that we picked, as I've talked about previously, there is really good competition for places. "There's not a lot between certain positions." Beaten All Blacks climb above Springboks Eddie James started alongside Max Llewellyn for the second time for Wales [Press Association] New Zealand still inched above South Africa, who lost a thriller in France on Friday, into top spot in the southern hemisphere table. If the All Blacks win with a bonus point at Twickenham on Saturday (14:10 GMT), they will secure top spot before the Springboks' game in Ireland (20:10 GMT). "It hurts, but you've got to take it on the chin," said Rennie, who took over from Scott Robertson at the start of the year. "We weren't good enough; Wales were passionate and every time they kept us out, they grew and became harder to break down. "We've got to be better, we expect a lot more of ourselves, and I need to see a response at Twickenham."

item.title: Bears Paid High Price For Simmons, But He Is The Real Prize
item.description: Talia Sprague-Imagn Images The Chicago Bears did not wait until the final hours of the trade deadline to make their move. They secured the best defensive player in the NFL two weeks before the deadline arrived. To acquire All-Pro defensive tackle Jeffery Simmons, General Manager Ryan Poles traded two first-round picks to the Tennessee Titans, according to Bleacher Nation . The Simmons trade stands apart from every other transaction that happened this week. While other teams swapped veterans for late picks, Chicago bought a cornerstone for the next four years. The Cost of a Game-Wrecker The price tag drew immediate criticism from some analysts. The Bears received a C grade from ESPN, which contended that the team exceeded the point where the compensation remained sensible. That cost comprised the 2027 and 2028 first-round picks alongside a 2027 fourth-rounder. The team did get a 2028 fifth-round pick back. But the value lies in who Simmons is, not just the draft capital spent. He is 29 years old and a four-time Pro Bowler. After logging a career-high 11 sacks last season, he secured his first first-team All-Pro nod. Prior to the trade, ESPN listed him as the interior lineman with the highest pass rush win rate. Seth Walder and Ben Solak at ESPN called him the best defensive tackle in the league, period. That assessment carries weight when looking at the rest of the board. Simmons Versus The Rest Other teams made moves for players who are past their prime. Kirk Cousins is now a Viking. Keenan Allen is a 49er. Josh Downs is in Kansas City. Marvin Harrison Jr. is in Houston. Jessie Bates is in Jacksonville. The best counterargument points to DeForest Buckner, who the 49ers landed for a 2027 fourth-round pick. Buckner is 32 and currently in the final year of his contract. This season, his pass rush win rate has fallen to the 45th percentile. That is down from the 90th percentile a year ago. He is a nice rental for a contender. Simmons is a player you build around for years. The 49ers paid for a few months of a good player. The Bears paid for years of a great one. The contract situation adds another layer to the deal. The Titans had recently extended Simmons and had already paid the bonus. Consequently, Chicago owes him $7.94 million for the remainder of this season plus $26.95 million in future guarantees. Chicago now possesses a player who has accumulated 10 tackles, including three tackles for loss, in only two games. He has also recorded two sacks, two QB hits, and two pass breakups. His presence has demanded double teams, which opens the door for teammates like Montez Sweat and Austin Booker to feast. The Bears are 7-2 and sit atop the NFC North. If they keep winning, those two first-round picks will land somewhere in the high 20s.

item.title: Eagles’ Howie Roseman Turns Heads With Darian Mensah Interaction
item.description: Philadelphia Eagles general manager Howie Roseman was in town to watch Miami standout quarterback Darian Mensah in person this week as the Hurricanes take on Duke. What makes that such a storyline? Well, the Eagles are facing an uncertain future with current franchise quarterback Jalen Hurts. Hurts was forced to end his season early due to multiple issues with blood clots. Hurts is facing an uncertain future himself. There are some who believe that he is facing an uphill battle to play football again. If the blood clot issues persist, he will need to stay on blood thinners, which would effectively end his ability to play football. Of course, all of that is pure speculation. No one truly knows what the future has in store for Hurts in Philadelphia. With that being said, if the Eagles do end up needing another quarterback, Roseman could target one in the 2027 NFL Draft. That has led to speculation about Mensah being a potential option, especially after Roseman was seen interacting with the young signal caller this week. Philadelphia Eagles general manager Howie Roseman looks on before the game against the Los Angeles Chargers at SoFi Stadium. Mandatory Credit: Kirby Lee-Imagn Images Eagles GM Howie Roseman’s Darian Mensah Interaction Causes Stir NFL insider Jordan Schultz was the first to share a video of Roseman on the field with Mensah . It didn’t take long for fans to begin talking about the interaction. “Maybe Jalen’s replacement?” one fan questioned . Another chimed in , “Geez no wonder why Howie is stacking them picks.” “Mensah would set the Eagles franchise back 10 years. Oof. Did he not watch CJ Carr Saturday night?” a third fan wrote . Mensah has been one of the most productive quarterbacks in college football this season. So far this year, he has completed 76.8 percent of his pass attempts for 2,694 yards, 28 touchdowns, and two interceptions. He has also picked up 137 yards and scored two touchdowns on the ground. Whether or not the Eagles are actually interested in Mensah in the 2027 NFL Draft remains to be seen. Roseman could simply be doing his due diligence. Regardless of the interest level, seeing Roseman interacting with Mensah personally has caused some reaction from the Philadelphia fan base. item.title: Five Stars Burn 2027 Tour Cards After Austin Cut Blunder
item.description: Aug 1, 2026; Detroit, Michigan, USA; Peter Malnati chips onto the 18th green during the third round of the Rocket Classic golf tournament. Mandatory Credit: Aaron Doster-Imagn Images The race for 2027 PGA Tour cards turned ugly in Austin on Saturday. Five high-profile players missed the cut at the Austin Championship, a mistake that could cost them their status for next season. The cut line sat at 4 under par at the Fazio Canyons course, leaving no room for error. These five names are now in a panic as they look at their futures. Per Golfweek, the stakes were massive for anyone trying to lock up a card . The winner takes home a $1.08 million check, but the real prize is staying inside the top 100 in the FedEx Cup standings. Missing the weekend in Austin means losing precious points that might have saved a career. The pressure during the FedEx Cup Fall is intense, and these players cracked under it. The Cost of One Bad Swing Scottie Scheffler isn’t the one in trouble, but Thompson is. Sitting at No. 94 as the week began, he stood right on the edge of keeping full status. Thompson needed a simple par on his final hole Friday to survive. Instead, he knocked his approach shot into the water and made a bogey. That single swing cost him the weekend and put his card in jeopardy. Never catching up after recording a bogey on each of the first two holes, Malnati fell behind. His second round was clean with no bogeys, but he only made two birdies. That was not enough to reach the cut line. He now sits just outside the number needed to get tiered conditional status. One bad start can ruin an entire season for players on the bubble. Two Weeks of Bad Golf Moore had a great run at Bermuda with a third-place finish, but that momentum is gone. He has now missed two consecutive cuts at a time when he cannot afford to lose ground. Moore opened his second round with three bogeys in the first four holes. He fell on the wrong side of the line because his closing round included two additional bogeys. Kirk thought Austin was a great spot to climb back into the top 100. With two consecutive over-par rounds, he is now going in the wrong direction. Pendrith started on the back nine and went three over in his first four holes. He fought hard to get back to the cutline but could not make it. What looked like a golden opportunity has now fallen away for all of them. The Road Ahead Is Rough These five players now face a much harder path to keep their Tour cards . They must perform well in the remaining FedEx Cup Fall events to make up for the lost points. The window to fix this mistake is closing fast as the season moves toward its end. Per Golfweek, the cut line at 4 under par was a wall they could not climb. The tournament finished Saturday morning at the Omni Barton Creek Resort. The players who missed the cut must hope their next start is much better. The 2027 season depends on how they handle this pressure in the coming weeks.

item.title: Why Urban Meyer is buying in to 24-team CFP expansion
item.description: Jerome Miron-Imagn Images Why Urban Meyer is buying in to 24-team CFP expansion appeared first on ClutchPoints . Add ClutchPoints as a Preferred Source by clicking here . With the NCAA football landscape changing year-by-year, many fans and commentators have strong opinions about this shifting landscape. One of those changes is that the College Football Playoff will soon expand to 24 teams. Former college football coach Urban Meyer is okay with that . “My instant reaction is it’s not death if you lose,” Meyer said, per FOX. “…..Now you’re 12, and now 24. 24 if you lose, keep rolling.” The 24-team CFP is starting in 2027 and @CoachUrbanMeyer gives his thoughts pic.twitter.com/Eu5VyhoQHj Watch sports LIVE with fuboTV (free trial) — Big Noon Kickoff (@BNKonFOX) November 14, 2026 The CFP format has moved from four teams to now 12 teams. The field will expand again to 24 teams, starting in 2027. That certainly allows more programs an opportunity to compete for a national championship . “The 24-team field will be made up of four guaranteed spots for Power 4 conference champions (ACC, Big Ten, Big 12 and SEC), one guaranteed spot for the highest-ranked team from the Group of 6 leagues (American, Conference USA, MAC, Mountain West, Pac-12 and Sun Belt) and 19 at-large spots chosen by the selection committee. Seeds 1-8 will earn a first-round bye and host a second-round game on campus. Seeds 9-24 will play first-round games on the campus of the higher seed,” The Athletic reported about the expansion. Due to the playoff expanding, there are also changes coming to scheduling rules for power 4 college football teams. In order to qualify for a spot in the expanded playoff, those teams will have to play at least 10 other power 4 schools each year. That includes conference opponents, and then teams from other power 4 leagues or Notre Dame. It appears that this latest expansion might be the last new change for a while with the CFP. “A move to a 24-team field in 2027 will mark five consecutive years with a change to the Playoff’s layout or format, but with this latest deal, talk of expansion is off the table for the near future,” The Athletic reported. College Football Playoff games for this season begin in mid-December. item.title: Avalanche Lose MacKinnon for Extended Time, Makar for Two Weeks
item.description: USA TODAY Sports via Reuters Connect The Colorado Avalanche will be without superstars Nathan MacKinnon and Cale Makar for an extended period. Avalanche head coach Jared Bednar told reporters in Montreal on Saturday morning that MacKinnon is out for at least a month, while Makar is expected to miss two weeks. Both players suffered lower-body injuries in Ottawa, with the incidents occurring around a minute apart in the second period. To replace MacKinnon in the lineup , Colorado recalled forward Gavin Brindley from the American Hockey League on Saturday. The Denver Post’s Corey Masisak confirmed that Brock Nelson will move up to the top line in MacKinnon’s absence, while Nic Roy will center a line with Gabe Landeskog . Nazem Kadri will center another line. On defense, rookie Alex Gagne will make his NHL debut alongside Brent Burns, who is set to appear in his 1,600th career regular-season game. That likely means Noah Juulsen moves up to play with Brett Kulak, leaving Devon Toews and Sam Malinski together as the top pair. The top power play will also have Toews and Artturi Lehkonen on it. They’ll join Martin Necas, T.J. Hughes, and Kadri, as they did after Thursday’s injuries . MacKinnon is Colorado’s top point producer, recording 10 goals, 20 assists, and 30 points in 20 games this season. Makar, who previously missed a game for the birth of his twin children, has five goals and 23 points in 19 games. This is a rare situation for Colorado. Saturday’s matchup against the Canadiens will mark just the seventh time that both superstars have been unavailable for the same game since Makar made his NHL debut. It’s also the first time since March 2021 that both players will miss the same game outside of occasional late-season rest ahead of the playoffs. Bednar said Makar’s injury is soft tissue-related and that there is no concern it will linger beyond the current recovery timeline. The timing offers the Avalanche at least a little relief. Colorado has just five games scheduled over the next two weeks, meaning Makar could miss a relatively small portion of the schedule if he returns as expected. MacKinnon’s absence, however, is expected to stretch considerably longer. There’s no question that it’s going to be a challenge. item.title: Benatia: ‘Ronaldo asked me to speak to Allegri at Juventus about skipping pre-match retreats’
item.description: Benatia: ‘Ronaldo asked me to speak to Allegri at Juventus about skipping pre-match retreats’ Medhi Benatia has revealed how Cristiano Ronaldo’s dislike of pre-match retreats led to a conversation with Massimiliano Allegri during their time together at Juventus. With quotes via Calciomercato.com , the former Morocco defender told the story to Canal+. Italian clubs traditionally keep their squads together in a hotel or at the training ground the night before matches, known as the ritiro, and Ronaldo found it hard to adjust when he arrived from Real Madrid in 2018. “In 2018 Cristiano Ronaldo arrived, and he didn’t really like the ritiro because he wasn’t used to it,” Benatia said. “He said to me: ‘Isn’t there a way to talk to the Italians a bit, to the coach?’ I replied: ‘Yes, of course, we’ll try.’ “So I went to Chiellini and said: ‘Gio, there’s this teammate who doesn’t really appreciate the ritiro and everything that comes with it.’ He asked: ‘Why? Did he tell you that?’ I said: ‘Yes, he came to me.’ “So we went to speak to the coach, Allegri at the time, together with Chiellini: ‘Mister, there are three or four players, especially the big players, who would prefer not to do the ritiro, if possible.’ The coach replied: ‘Whoever wants to go on the ritiro goes, whoever doesn’t want to doesn’t go.’” TURIN, ITALY – AUGUST 14: Cristiano Ronaldo of Juventus looks on during the pre-season friendly match between Juventus and Atalanta BC at Allianz Stadium on August 14, 2021 in Turin, Italy. (Photo by Emilio Andreoli/Getty Images) Benatia on Ronaldo and his Juventus move Benatia spent two and a half years with the Bianconeri, from 2016 to January 2019, winning two Scudetti, two Coppa Italia titles and a Supercoppa Italiana. He joined from Bayern Munich, where he never settled. “I wanted to leave after the first year, so I asked to go. I wanted to come back to Italy. Juve, Inter and other clubs were interested,” he explained. “After two months in Germany, I said to my wife: ‘Listen, I don’t know if I made the right choice here. I don’t feel comfortable. Italy is my second home.’ Medhi Benatia (@m.benatia5 via Instagram) “So I came back and joined Juve. That’s when you see how important work culture and discipline are.”

item.title: Olid hails goalscorer Le Tissier on 150th Man Utd appearance
item.description: Olid hails goalscorer Le Tissier on 150th Man Utd appearance Manchester United Women boss Eva Olid hailed Maya Le Tissier after the defender marked her 150th appearance for the club with a goal in their 2-0 win over Crystal Palace. Le Tissier became only the fifth player to reach 150 appearances for United Women, following Ella Toone, Katie Zelem, Millie Turner and Leah Galton. “That is incredible, no?” Olid said after her team’s WSL victory. “Because for a defender you expect the minimum. You need to defend well and help to build. “But now she’s scoring goals and that is more than a manager can ask from a centre-back. “She’s at a high level and, yeah, I’m so happy for her.” Elisabeth Terland added a second to secure the victory for United, who have now kept four clean sheets in a row. “That [clean sheets] was the focus from the first two matches. We say we cannot just focus in attack and the fact that we concede goals in the first two games made us be so demanding that we need to keep the clean sheet,” Olid explained. “At the same time we can enjoy attacking and trying to create chances, but it is so important that we keep that clean sheet.”

item.title: NFL Rumors: Green Bay Packers Pursued Trade for Starting RB, Balked at Club’s High Asking Price
item.description: IMAGN IMAGES via Reuters Connect The Green Bay Packers have the worst rushing offense in the NFL this season, ranking last in rushing yards per game (68.2) with the second-lowest yards per carry average (3.0). Hoping to improve things with Josh Jacobs out multiple weeks, general manager Brian Gutekunst reportedly pursued a deal for a new starting running back. According to ESPN ‘s Adam Schefter, Green Bay and the Denver Broncos both inquired with the Tennessee Titans regarding the availability of running back Tony Pollard. Tennessee was open to dealing the 29-year-old running back, who is in a contract year, but the asking price reportedly pushed Green Bay and Denver away. Tony Pollard stats (2026): 595 rushing yards, 6 rushing touchdowns, 4.5 yards per carry The Titans front office made it clear that Pollard wouldn’t be moved for anything less than a third-round pick. From Tennessee’s perspective, Pollard’s recent stretch of success (322 rushing yards and 5.0 yards per carry in last three games) was instrumental in the improved play as of late from quarterback Cam Ward. Unless Green Bay or Denver was willing to overpay for a half season of Pollard, a deal wouldn’t be made. It’s the second running back Green Bay has been connected to in NFL trade rumors. Even before Jacobs’ injury, the Packers reportedly inquired with the Indianapolis Colts regarding All-Pro running back Jonathan Taylor. While he was technically available, Indianapolis wanted a first-round pick for him or multiple Day 2 picks in the 2027 NFL Draft and future draft capital. The Micah Parsons trade leaves Green Bay without a first-round pick in the 2027 NFL Draft. Gutekunst’s draft capital took another blow this week when the Miami Dolphins placed quarterback Malik Willis on injured reserve. Because he’s now expected to miss at least four games, the projected third-round compensatory pick Green Bay anticipated receiving for Miami signing him will likely now be a fourth-round selection in 2027. Ultimately, Gutekunst just couldn’t justify sacrificing all of his Day 2 picks and additional assets for Taylor nor was he willing to give up a third-round pick for half a season of Pollard. Given that Green Bay’s offensive line has been one of the biggest reasons for the run game’s struggles, that could prove to be the right decision. item.title: RAF Abu Dhabi results: Merab Dvalishvili’s teammate Saba Lazashvili pulls off upset win over Urijah Faber
item.description: Saba Lazashvili rallies to win debut at RAF Abu Dhabi. | RAF It’s been quite a week for Saba Lazashvili. Prior to Wednesday, he was an unknown Georgian wrestler and teammate to Merab Dvalishvili but after backing up the former UFC bantamweight champion when they were attacked by Usman Nurmagomegdov and members of his squad, the 21-year-old has suddenly become a household name. On Saturday, Lazashvili not only competed at RAF Abu Dhabi on short notice but he pulled off an upset win over former WEC champion Urijah Faber. This is where Saba Lazishvili turned the tables after losing the first two periods, showing his wrestling skills in the third to secure an incredible comeback victory. 🔥 Via: @RAFWrestlingUSA pic.twitter.com/6jGf0hwA5a — FREAK.MMA (@FREAKMMA1) November 14, 2026 Down early in the match, Lazashvili stormed back in the third period after securing a takedown and then turning Faber several times to rack up a lot of points. In the end, Lazshvili went up 12-7 and Faber just couldn’t mount enough offense to prevent the loss. “I want to say thank you to everybody coming here and supporting,” Lazashvili said after his win.”I’m really grateful for everything. [Merab] said I will be champion of the UFC in the future! I’ll wrestle everybody here.” It was an ultra impressive showing, especially considering that Lazashvili wasn’t even supposed to compete when he arrived in Abu Dhabi but him taking out members of Nurmagomedov’s team during that brawl suddenly made him incredibly popular. Now, he’s a winner in RAF, and it’s hard to believe this is the last major opportunity that Lazashvili receives in the aftermath of that brawl.

item.title: Atiku tackles FG as bakers lose 40% membership
item.description: By Luminous Jannamike, Abuja Former Vice President Atiku Abubakar has blamed President Bola Tinubu’s economic policies for the loss of nearly 40 per cent of the membership of the Premium Breadmakers Association of Nigeria in two years, warning that soaring energy costs and high interest rates are driving local businesses out of operation. The development, he said, underscores the growing strain on businesses, with bakeries shutting down, workers losing their jobs and households paying more for bread, one of Nigeria’s everyday staples. Atiku, who was in Bauchi on Saturday to promote his affordable life campaign and sympathise with Nigerians grappling with the effects of government policies, spoke in a statement signed by his Director of Strategic Communication, ADC Presidential Campaign Council, and Senior Special Assistant on Public Communication, Phrank Shaibu. “From farmers to manufacturers and now bakers, the verdict on Tinubu’s economic reforms cannot be clearer: they have been a monumental failure,” he said. The former vice president identified rising energy costs and expensive credit as major constraints on bakery operations, noting that energy alone accounts for about half of production costs. He cited the case of a bakery operator whose monthly diesel bill reportedly increased from N9 million to N19 million, while small-scale bakeries require between N40 million and N50 million to switch to alternative energy sources. He added that businesses seeking loans face interest rates of up to 34 per cent, further limiting their ability to sustain production and invest in more efficient operations. Atiku said the pressure extends beyond the baking industry, citing rising cooking gas prices, which he said had reached N1,800 per kilogramme in Abuja and N1,650 in parts of Lagos and Ogun states. He also cited a 31.8 per cent increase in depot prices within one month, from N1,100 to N1,450 per kilogramme. Turning to the Federal Government’s borrowing, Atiku questioned the accumulation of domestic and foreign loans amid the reported closure of local businesses, alleging that Nigerians were yet to see tangible benefits from the debt. “The irony is that while the economy is falling under Bola Tinubu’s watch, his government has accumulated local and foreign loans in astronomical figures. If local businesses are dying while the government continues to borrow, Nigerians are entitled to ask where these loans are going. One is forced to conclude that they are feeding the corruption in Tinubu’s government,” he said. He called for a shift in economic priorities towards strengthening domestic production across sectors, rather than concentrating exclusively on crude oil refining. “The major policy plank of my administration will be to improve local production in every sphere of the economy, not just crude oil refining. “To farmers, manufacturers, bakers and everyone involved in local production: the Atiku Economic Recovery Plan understands your pains, and your con

item.title: Spain will host 2030 World Cup final, federation president insists
item.description: The 2030 World Cup final will be in Spain, Spanish Football Federation (RFEF) head Rafael Louzan reiterated on Saturday, adding that he is not considering “withdrawing” should he be wrong. Spain is organising the next World Cup with Portugal and Morocco. The decision on the venue for the final will be made in 2028, Louzan said. Spain favours Real Madrid’s Santiago Bernabeu Stadium for the final. Portugal does not have a suitable stadium but Morocco has suggested the 115,000-capacity Hassan II Stadium being built in Benslimane near Casablanca. “There is no other plan than for the final to be held in Spain,” said Louzan at a conference at the RFEF’s Ciudad del Futbol on the outskirts of Madrid. “I am not currently considering the possibility of withdrawing from Spain, as the prospect of Spain not hosting the final is not on the table,” he said. Louzan was responding to Alberto Nunez Feijoo, the leader of the right-wing People’s Party. In a television interview on November 5, Feijoo said that were he to become prime minister in the general election on November 29, he would advocate withdrawing Spain’s bid to host the World Cup should Morocco be awarded the final. Luzon said the question was entirely hypothetical. “That notion simply doesn’t exist,” he said, adding that under FIFA’s tradition of rotating the World Cup the staging of the final “belongs to the European continent”. A delegation of FIFA technical experts spent last week visiting Spanish stadiums that are hoping to host matches during the tournament, Louzan said. The post Spain will host 2030 World Cup final, federation president insists appeared first on Vanguard News .

item.title: 2027: I’ll restore fuel subsidy, tackle insecurity if elected — Atiku vows
item.description: By Christopher Ameh, Bauchi & Ayobami Okerinde Former Vice-President and presidential candidate of the African Democratic Congress (ADC) Atiku Abubakar has promised to restore fuel subsidy and tackle insecurity if elected president. Atiku made the pledge on Saturday during the ADC presidential campaign rally in Bauchi State, where he urged residents to vote for candidates of the party across all elective positions. “I have already promised all Nigerians that I will restore petroleum subsidy. Not only that, I will also restore subsidy in electricity,” he said. Atiku also pledged to address insecurity in the Northeast and other parts of the country, while promising to expand petroleum exploration in the Kolmani area to generate additional revenue. He called on Nigerians to support the ADC, urging voters in Bauchi to elect the party’s candidates from the presidency to the councillorship positions. The former vice-president thanked the people of the state for their previous support, saying Bauchi had consistently given him substantial votes in past elections. He urged residents to turn out in large numbers during the 2027 polls and ensure their votes were protected and counted. “I want you to make sure you come out in your thousands. You vote for ADC. You defend the vote. You ensure that the votes are counted, and results are transmitted before you leave the polling booth,” Atiku said. President Bola Tinubu announced the removal of petrol subsidy on May 29, 2023, during his inauguration, declaring that “the fuel subsidy is gone”. He said the funds would instead be redirected to infrastructure, education, healthcare and job creation. Atiku has repeatedly promised to restore petrol subsidy if elected in 2027. In August , he reiterated the pledge, questioning how the savings from its removal had been spent. The former vice president was accompanied by his running mate and former Minister of Transportation, Rotimi Amaechi, ADC National Chairman, Senator David Mark, and other party leaders, said his administration would prioritise policies aimed at alleviating the economic hardship confronting Nigerians. Also associated with the Bauchi campaign delegation was the party’s governorship candidate in the state, Senator Halliru Dauda Jika, alongside other ADC chieftains and political stakeholders. The post 2027: I’ll restore fuel subsidy, tackle insecurity if elected — Atiku vows appeared first on Vanguard News .

item.title: Forgive Me If You Didn’t See Me In The hinterlands,’ Tinubu Tells Plateau Attack Victims
item.description: President Bola Tinubu has asked families affected by the deadly attacks in Anguwan Rukuba , in Jos North Local Government Area of Plateau State that left many killed and several injured in March 2026, to forgive him for not visiting the communities. ﻿ Tinubu spoke at the All Progressives Congress (APC) North-Central presidential campaign rally in Jos on Saturday. “When I last visited the other time, I was limited to the airport. Forgive me if you didn’t see me in the hinterland. But I saw the devastation; I got the report from the governor. I saw horror in the faces of our people. “But since then, that has changed; we are forging together. He, however, assured residents that their communities would be rebuilt for those displaced to return home. Tinubu said too many lives had been lost to attacks in Plateau since 2001. He condoled with families who have lost loved ones to such attacks. Tinubu, who is seeking re-election on the platform of the All Progressives Congress (APC), called for unity, saying speaking different languages should not lead to divisions. “I have directed all the security agencies to take decisive action and sustain peace and stability on the Plateau. “What we should be getting is prosperity, not havoc, not crisis. Our government is not elected to inflict wounds on one another or to bury people. We have to lift people up from penury to prosperity. “One thousand forest guards are undergoing training right now. You will feel them; you will see them. You will feel secure in your villages and communities,” he added. The President also said the surveillance cameras had been procured as promised. Tinubu assured the residents that his government his working to ease their suffering. A deadly attack in Anguwan Rukuba, in Jos North Local Government Area of the state in March, 2026, left at least 20 people killed and many others injured. On April 2, Tinubu met with the affected families at the Jos Airport, where he condoled with them and assured them that such an incident would not recur. ﻿ The President was criticised for not visiting the affected communities, but his spokesperson, Bayo Onanuga , said that said the visit was affected by a scheduled meeting with the President of Chad. item.title: Kwankwaso’s daughter seeks divorce from Kano gov, offers to refund dowry
item.description: By Hadiza Yusuf The second wife of Kano State Governor, Abba Kabir Yusuf, Zainab Musa Kwankwaso, has filed for divorce at an Upper Area Court in Gudu, Abuja, offering to refund the dowry paid by the governor. Zainab, a daughter of former Kano State Governor Senator Rabiu Musa Kwankwaso, is seeking to dissolve the marriage through Khul’i, an Islamic procedure that allows a woman to seek divorce by returning her dowry or offering compensation. According to court documents, the court has summoned Governor Yusuf to appear on November 17, 2026, to respond to the suit. In her claim, Zainab cited a breakdown of the marriage, alleging a persistent lack of love, care, affection and emotional connection. She also told the court that efforts to reconcile them had failed and expressed willingness to refund the dowry paid on their wedding day. Zainab married Yusuf on July 29, 2006, and their marriage produced six children. Her divorce suit comes weeks after she reportedly left the Kano Government House for her father’s residence before travelling to Abuja. item.title: 2027: We won’t allow religion to divide us, Makinde declares
item.description: …seeks Muslim community’s support for Adekanmbi By Adeola Badru Oyo State Governor and presidential candidate of the Allied Peoples Movement (APM), ‘Seyi Makinde, has declared that his administration will not allow religious differences to divide the people of the state, insisting that they share a common ancestry and must remain united irrespective of their faith. Makinde, who made the declaration on Saturday, also appealed to Muslim leaders across the state to use their influence to promote unity, peace and political stability ahead of the 2027 general elections. The governor spoke at the opening of a three-day conference for Imams, Alfas/Ulama, political office holders and traditional rulers, tagged Rabitah 2026, organised by the League of Imams and Alfas in Yoruba Land (Rabitah tul Aimma wal Hulammai fii Biladi Yoruba) at the Jogor Event Centre, Ibadan. The conference, with the theme, “The Responsibilities of Politicians and Electorate During and After Electoral Process,“ brought together prominent Islamic clerics, scholars, traditional rulers and political stakeholders from across the South-West. Makinde noted that discussions surrounding the choice of the next governor of the state had intensified ahead of the elections, urging political and religious stakeholders not to allow such developments to create divisions along religious lines. “We won’t allow religion to divide us. Let us pray for our state and country because this is the period leading to the next election, when a new set of leaders will emerge.“ “There is a lot of discussion going on right now about the choice of who will become the next governor.“ “What matters most is that we must stay united. The progress of Oyo State is what is important to us, and I believe God will answer our prayers. For us in Oyo State, religion is not an issue.“ “We have all religions in our various families, and we have always coexisted peacefully,” he said. Makinde further illustrated the historical and familial connections between Muslims and Christians in Oyo State, disclosing that his own family background reflected the religious diversity he was advocating. He said: “I, standing before you, am Oluseyi Makinde. “Makinde was my grandfather on my father’s side. My father’s name is Olatunbosun, and my grandfather, Makinde, lived and died as a Muslim. Those who are familiar with Oyo know this history.“ “If I were to convene an extended family meeting this evening, about 65 per cent of those who would attend would be Muslims.“ “I want to appeal to us that we must not allow ourselves to be divided along religious lines because we share the same ancestry and the same blood flows through our veins.” The governor urged participants at the conference to use the gathering to pray for the continued peace and development of the state, stressing that religious differences should not undermine the bonds that unite the people. “Therefore, as this conference progresses, let us pray and work towards sustaining our u
