item.title: Scientists warn 1.5°C climate change threshold could arrive by 2029
item.description: ANTALYA, Turkey—Amid upbeat green-tech pep talks and notices for happy hours at the annual United Nations COP31 climate change conference on Thursday, two new reports offered a stark reminder of how far the world remains from containing global warming. Climate Action Tracker , a nonprofit group that analyzes climate policies, found that the planet is still on track to warm nearly 5° Fahrenheit by 2100, a rise that would devastate coral reefs, disrupt agriculture and forests and melt most of the world’s ice. In a separate bulletin, the European Union’s Copernicus climate change service reported that global warming has accelerated significantly since the 2015 Paris climate agreement . When the Paris agreement was adopted, the average global temperature was projected to surpass the pact’s long-term threshold of 2.7° Fahrenheit above the preindustrial average around 2045. After another decade of global climate summits, warming is now projected to cross that benchmark as soon as 2029, according to Copernicus. Read full article Comments

item.title: Bitcoin Price Briefly Crashes to $67,500, Lowest Since August, as Dollar Holds 19-Month High
item.description: Bitcoin Magazine Bitcoin Price Briefly Crashes to $67,500, Lowest Since August, as Dollar Holds 19-Month High Bitcoin price traded near $69,800 on Friday morning after briefly crashing to about $67,555 around midnight Eastern, its lowest level since mid-August, according to Bitcoin Magazine Pro data. The rebound held after October producer prices rose less than economists had expected, though the U.S. dollar remained near a 19-month high and traders still fully priced a December Federal Reserve rate hike. Bitcoin price was trading near $72,800 at this time Thursday. It slipped toward $71,000 by Thursday evening, then gave way late at night, breaking below $70,000 and sliding to that midnight low. The move also pushed the bitcoin price below its 200-week moving average , a long-term trend line near $68,000. Buyers lifted it back above $69,000 before sunrise, and the rebound extended toward $69,800 after the producer-price report. A stronger dollar and higher yields weigh on the bitcoin price The U.S. Dollar Index held above 103 Friday after a three-day rally took it to its highest level since April 2025. The 10-year Treasury yield was near 5.15% ahead of the data, and two-year yields, which track Fed expectations most closely, were on pace for their worst week since 2024, Bloomberg reported. Traders still see an 88% chance of a quarter-point hike at the Fed’s Dec. 8-9 meeting and a 12% chance of a half-point move, CME FedWatch data show . Fed Governor Christopher Waller has added a 50-basis-point increase to the discussion, and New York Fed President John Williams said Thursday that inflation remains high and policymakers need to take further action. Higher rates raise the cost of holding an asset that pays no interest, and a stronger dollar tends to drain demand for risk assets. Both have pressured the bitcoin price since this week’s hotter-than-expected consumer price index. Bitcoin has also broken from tech stocks. It fell 5.9% between Nov. 5 and Nov. 12 while the Nasdaq 100 gained 6.4%, a sign it is trading more on yields and the dollar than on the AI trade. Nasdaq 100 futures were up about 0.6% Friday after the producer-price report, as investors also weighed Nvidia’s announcement that Jensen Huang had resigned as CEO. Leverage unwinds and ETF selling continues The break below $70,000 set off a wave of forced selling. About $1.64 billion in crypto positions were liquidated over 24 hours, with bets on higher prices making up nearly 89% of the total and bitcoin positions accounting for $916 million. U.S. spot bitcoin ETFs added to the pressure. The funds posted about $47.7 million in net outflows Thursday, their sixth straight day of withdrawals, bringing the run to roughly $1.49 billion. BlackRock’s iShares Bitcoin Trust (IBIT) alone bled about $2 billion over nine sessions through Wednesday, and the group has now flipped to about $1.56 billion in net outflows for 2026. Sentiment has soured with it. A widely watched crypto fear and greed gauge

item.title: Oh my Word! Microsoft retires compatibility options, because who needs layouts to stay put
item.description: Microsoft is retiring some legacy layout settings in Word, potentially rearranging documents created or last saved in Word 2010 or earlier. "Affected documents may show layout differences, such as text reflow, changes in spacing or page count, or images and shapes moving to another page," the Windows biz said . The advice, if silly little things like page layout in a document matter, is to "consider exporting it to PDF before the change." Compatibility Mode lets a newer version of Word open a document created in an older version, such as Word 2010, without changing its layout. Newer features are switched off while the document is open this way. Users can convert the document to unlock newer features, although people using older versions of Word may then have difficulty editing parts of it. Microsoft has not identified the individual settings being retired, saying only: "We are retiring a set of compatibility options in Microsoft Word (desktop app) for documents in Compatibility Mode." The reason? "To simplify how Word handles document layout and provide a more consistent experience across platforms." Administrators may therefore want to check older templates, forms, and other documents whose pagination needs to stay put. The change is due to begin rolling out in the Windows version of Word from December 2026 and be completed by January 2027. The Mac version will follow in early 2027. Microsoft Word is more than 40 years old, and its first Windows version was released as the 1980s drew to a close. The word processor has evolved over the decades and is a mainstay of Microsoft's productivity suite. Compatibility Mode helps keep older documents from having their layouts abruptly borked the way Word does so well . Losing some of those safeguards could give administrators a fresh batch of "what the heck has happened to this document?" tickets as the change rolls out. ®

item.title: Quantum Systems drones back in the air after malware scare
item.description: Quantum Systems says its drones are flying again with Germany's military after a cyberattack prompted a precautionary grounding. The company says it spotted the attack at the end of October and reported it to the relevant authorities, but disclosed few details about the intrusion. "The threat was contained thanks to the swift response of our IT and security teams in close and transparent collaboration with the authorities," it said on Thursday. "Through the quick measures taken and the characteristics of the incident, there is no risk in operating Quantum Systems' unmanned systems for the end users and the operators." It added that other players in the European defense industry, and those who support Ukraine's military efforts, have faced "persistent cyberattacks for years." The Bundeswehr grounded its Quantum Systems drones after malware was detected in an update to QBase, the company's QBase ground-control software, Der Spiegel reported, citing unnamed sources. QBase lets operators plan missions, monitor flights, and process data from the ground. The malicious update reportedly reached servers belonging to the German military and other customers, but did not directly infect the drones. "The fleet is operating normally around the globe – including Germany and the Bundeswehr," Quantum Systems told Reuters . "The Bundeswehr was the only customer to ground their systems as a precaution." A spokesperson for Germany's defense ministry declined to comment on the attack or the reported details. The Register asked Quantum Systems for further details. Founded in 2015, Quantum Systems has been providing drones to the Ukrainian war effort for years. Last month, Chancellor Friedrich Merz announced funding for "several tens of thousands" of the company's interceptor drones as part of Germany's winter aid package. The new drones will be built in Ukraine and support interceptor systems already in use on the front lines. Quantum Systems announced a $1.2 billion Series D funding round in July, valuing the company at around $8 billion. ®

item.title: FWIFT 2026 Convention Communique: Industry Leaders Charge Women in Media to Embrace Cross-Border Growth
item.description: The Forum for Women in Film and Television Nigeria (FWIFT) successfully concluded its 2026 annual convention on Thursday, October 29, at the historic Glover Memorial Hall in Lagos, Nigeria. Convening under the theme “One Industry, Many Voices: Building Together,” the afternoon brought together over 200 practitioners from several sectors including; film, television, radio, advertising, and digital media to connect, share insights, and build mutual agency. Supported by the African Women’s Development Fund (AWDF) , the convention featured a keynote address by cultural curator Sandra Mbanefo Obiago , interactive panel sessions, break-out workshops, speed networking, and a flagship fireside chat titled “The Cross Over: A Career Beyond Borders.” The event drew leading voices from across the creative economy, including media executive Kadaria Ahmed , filmmaker Biodun Stephens, media personality Gbemi Olateru-Olagbegi, executive director Rosemary Egabor-Afolahan, and director Esosa Osagiede. Key takeaways and actionable resolutions from the convention sessions emphasized resilience, strategic partnerships, and structural evolution: Embrace Bold Collaboration and Risk-Taking: Speakers urged media professionals to shed apprehension around institutional partnerships. As highlighted during the panel discussions: “Do not allow fear of failing stop you from asking for help, do your due diligence on the people you want to partner with then go for it. If it does not work, do not stop, get up and go again.” Adaptability as a Survival Imperative: In an era of rapid technological and digital shifts across broadcast and film, participants were reminded of the absolute necessity of evolution: “If you don’t change with the times, you will grow stale.” Deconstructing Industry Myths: Addressing professional dynamics, panelists challenged antiquated narratives regarding female competition, affirming that systemic progress relies on solidarity: “Women work well with women, it is a myth that they do not.” FWIFT’s leadership noted that the conversations at Glover Memorial Hall mark a critical step toward cementing cross-sector alliances. The forum remains committed to translating these insights into actionable frameworks, mentorship programs, and policy advocacy for women shaping the future of African media. For more information on upcoming FWIFT initiatives, programs, and future events, visit the official website or follow @fwiftnigeria on social media. About FWIFT Nigeria The Forum For Women in Film and Television Nigeria (FWIFT) is a professional organization dedicated to empowering Nigerian women in screen-based, audio, and digital media through advocacy, skill acquisition, mentorship, and strategic networking. Media Contact: Forum of Women in Film and Television Nigeria (FWIFT) Email: fwiftnigeria@gmail.com | Website . item.title: Double-catch drama: Why Starship's Flight 15 is so important to SpaceX
item.description: null Update for 6:25 p.m. ET: SpaceX has launched the Starship Flight 15 mission, but did skip the first stage Super Heavy booster landing. See launch video and our full Starship Flight 15 liftoff wrap . Having reached orbit for the first time with Starship last time out, SpaceX is looking to take a huge stride toward full reusability with Flight 15 — the first attempt to catch the megarocket's Ship upper stage, as the company eyes hourly launches by 2030. SpaceX is targeting today (Nov. 13) for Starship 's 15th flight, which will lift off from the company's Starbas site in South Texas. If all goes well, the mission — which you can watch here at Space.com — will end on Saturday (Nov. 14) with the first attempt at what SpaceX itself calls the "Holy Grail of rocketry": Catching both Starship's Super Heavy booster and Ship upper stage chopstick-style back at the launch pad. "If successful, this will mark the first full recovery of an orbital launch system and a breakthrough moment in making Starship a reliable, rapidly reusable rocket," SpaceX wrote in its Flight 15 mission description . The 75-minute Flight 15 launch window opens today at 5:45 p.m. EST (2245 GMT), and a number of Starship firsts are planned for early in the flight. For example, while SpaceX has caught three Super Heavy boosters and reused two of them to date, the first attempt to catch a next-gen Super Heavy "V3" vehicle will come today, around 6.5 minutes after liftoff. If the Ship upper stage gets the go-ahead for orbital insertion, it will deploy 26 Starlink V3 satellites — designed especially for use on Starship — into low Earth orbit (LEO), starting about 35 minutes after launch. Then, 21 hours later, if "internally developed, and FAA-approved, conditions" for a return to Starbase and catch are met — including on-orbit assessment of Ship's heat shield by three of the V3 satellites — SpaceX will attempt to recover the orbital upper stage. This landmark try will follow the first-ever Ship reentry over inhabited areas, as the vehicle will maneuver its way over sparsely populated regions of northern Mexico and southern Texas. (On previous missions, Ship has splashed down in the open ocean.) It will head back to Starbase and make a bellyflop maneuver as it descends to the site's Pad 2 before flipping itself vertical, ready for embrace of the launch tower's waiting mechanical arms. "SpaceX will attempt to catch both the Super Heavy booster and Starship on the upcoming flight. If both are successful, it will mark the first time that all parts of an orbital rocket return to Earth intact," Elon Musk said via X, the social media platform he owns, on Nov. 6 . "This is the critical breakthrough needed to make life multiplanetary." Composite photo showing the Super Heavy booster of SpaceX's Starship megarocket coming in for a landing on the launch mount on Oct. 13, 2024. item.title: Palantir adds three UK police forces to its beat with £10.1M deal
item.description: Three UK police forces led by Cambridgeshire Constabulary have awarded Palantir a £10.1 million contract after London Mayor Sadiq Khan blocked a separate deal with the Metropolitan Police. The five-year agreement covers Bedfordshire Police, Cambridgeshire Constabulary, and Hertfordshire Constabulary, despite warnings from campaigners and politicians about dependence on the supplier. A contract award notice says the east of England police forces expect the Palantir platform to provide "an enterprise-wide data integration and analytics capability, enabling the secure ingestion, linking, and analysis of data from multiple systems and sources across the policing environment." The contract runs until October 2031, with the estimated value covering all three forces. News of the award coincided with revelations that former Metropolitan Police commissioner Dame Cressida Dick has worked as a paid adviser to Palantir since September 2025. A Palantir spokesperson told the Bureau of Investigative Journalism : "Dame Cressida is advising us on how our software could help improve the delivery of services in the public sector, drawing on more than 40 years of public service in a variety of roles." Dick said her role was limited to advising on how such products could assist public services. She said she had never lobbied or advocated for Palantir, or introduced the company to her contacts. Dick led the Metropolitan Police, the UK's largest force, between 2017 and 2022. She left after Khan said he had lost confidence in her. She later said she was " intimidated " into leaving. Separately, Khan stepped in to block the Met from awarding a £50 million contract to Palantir. His office cited serious concerns about the procurement process. Palantir later sued the Met, but the case was settled in October. The new police contract award follows a report from MPs warning of vendor lock-in to US suppliers, including Palantir. It said : "Our view that Palantir's increasing presence across the public sector represents an unacceptable point of weakness is not ideologically motivated or driven by concerns about the quality of their products. "The government should retain the ability to pick and choose individual suppliers and safeguard against the risk of vendor lock-in and debilitating dependencies, particularly in areas of critical national importance such as healthcare and national security infrastructure." ®

item.title: Digital Credit: Comparing The Six Bitcoin Preferred Stocks
item.description: Bitcoin Magazine Digital Credit: Comparing The Six Bitcoin Preferred Stocks Digital credit is an emerging asset class that transforms corporate Bitcoin balance sheets into income producing securities. Strategy pioneered the market with five perpetual preferred equity instruments: STRK, STRF, STRD, STRC, and STRE (the first four are listed in the U.S.). Strive subsequently introduced SATA and SATS, bringing the category to six U.S. instruments across two issuers. These securities offer investors preferred equity (read: credit-like) exposure to companies whose balance sheets are dominated by Bitcoin. Their perpetual structure means investors principally rely on recurring dividends and the continued financial strength of the issuer. Unlike term debt, there is no maturation date at which the full principal is ever paid back. Evaluating digital credit requires examining four characteristics: creditworthiness, investor protections, liquidity, and dividend profile. This article explains all four dimensions and then offers a ranking for the six digital credit instruments along these lines. None of this should be taken as investment advice—it is only a systematic framework for analyzing digital credit. 1. Creditworthiness Creditworthiness measures an issuer’s ability to support its financial obligations. Traditional credit analysis focuses on earnings, free cash flow, and refinancing capacity. Companies with strong cash generation can service interest and repay maturing debt. Digital credit issuers today derive financial strength primarily from their Bitcoin reserves, placing greater emphasis on net asset coverage. In the future we could certainly see digital credit issuers that also have significant cash flows on top of Bitcoin holdings, which would add to creditworthiness. The central question is how much Bitcoin supports each dollar of credit obligations. One useful measure is the BTC Rating , which compares the dollar value of Bitcoin reserves with the outstanding credit, accounting for the seniority of each credit instrument. Cash reserves can further strengthen creditworthiness by reducing net obligations. For example, a 5x BTC Rating indicates five dollars of Bitcoin supporting every dollar of notional credit claims. Higher ratings provide greater protection against Bitcoin price declines. Seniority matters because instruments from the same issuer can have different claims on the same asset base. A senior preferred instrument benefits from greater coverage than a junior preferred instrument: all senior claims are included in the BTC Rating calculation of a junior instrument. Creditworthiness also depends on corporate governance and capital allocation. Management must preserve sufficient Bitcoin coverage while funding recurring dividends. Issuing additional credit increases dividend obligations, while assets accumulation (Bitcoin or cash) strengthen the asset base. item.title: Ayobami Esther Akinnagbe: Organisational Mistakes Start-up Founders Should Avoid
item.description: Two women engaged in a professional meeting, discussing business in a modern office setting. Image by RDNE Stock project for Pexels . There is a lot that goes into establishing a successful business. It requires developing the business idea, securing clients, building a customer base and eventually bringing people on board. Starting a business and watching it grow can be an exciting experience. However, one thing many start-up founders overlook is the importance of having the right organisational structure in place. It is one thing to have a great business idea and attract talented employees, but it is another thing to create an environment where everyone understands their responsibilities, knows who they report to and can work effectively towards achieving the company’s objectives. I once worked with a client who needed a new set of employees for a business establishment that was reopening after a period of restructuring. As part of the recruitment process, the first thing I ensured was that a manager was hired before proceeding to fill the remaining vacancies. The idea was simple. The manager would oversee the day-to-day running of the establishment, ensure that company policies were implemented and periodically train employees based on the requirements of their respective roles. During the recruitment process, I clearly communicated each employee’s responsibilities and the person they would be reporting to. These details were also stated in their respective offer letters, so everyone understood their roles and the management structure they were expected to work within. However, there was a challenge. Before the manager was hired, an accountant who was personally known to both co-founders had also been in charge of the previous employees. Following the restructuring, the founders had communicated their desire for a new operational arrangement, and this was clearly reflected in the recruitment brief. Although the new employees understood that they were expected to report to the newly hired manager, the existing employees still had their loyalty to the accountant, who had previously been in charge. The challenge was that the new management structure had not been properly implemented within the organisation. Consequently, the manager was expected to take charge of the establishment without the necessary authority and cooperation from everyone involved. This created unnecessary friction, and I found myself having to mediate whenever issues arose, even though the service I had been engaged to provide was recruitment. I eventually had a lengthy conversation with one of the founders, explaining that communicating reporting lines and responsibilities during recruitment was only one part of the process. The organisation also needed to formally implement the new structure, clarify authority and ensure that everyone understood and respected the changes. Unfortunately, the founders believed they could figure things out themselves. Eventually, I had to dist

item.title: US university students tell surveillance cameras to Flock off
item.description: The privacy issues over the company’s surveillance cameras have caused protests in schools all over the country Angela Nguyen, a senior at Stanford University, has been on a mission to make sure her school doesn’t use automated license plate readers, like those made by Flock Safety, for mass surveillance. The 21-year-old computer science major helped collect hundreds of signatures earlier this year from students, faculty, alumni and residents to demand that Stanford drop its current Flock contract and codify safeguards for similar tech tools the school may use in the future. The fear, Nguyen says, is that these cameras, which show where a vehicle was at a certain point in time, can be exploited to victimize vulnerable people. Stanford cut ties with Flock this summer, and it’s not alone. The privacy reckoning over the company’s surveillance cameras is gaining momentum at schools nationwide. Since April, at least ten university campuses across seven states, have scrapped contracts with Flock. That includes Cornell University , Penn State University , Elgin Community College , Emory University , Binghamton University , Kent State University and the University of Wisconsin’s Madison , Milwaukee and Oshkosh branches. Last week, the University of Buffalo announced an indefinite pause on its plans for a 60-day pilot program. Continue reading...

item.title: Specialized’s Tarmac SL9 S-Level is built to wreck your Zone 2 ride
item.description: I love a good Zone 2 ride . There’s nothing like getting on the bike, settling into a groove, and letting the miles (and hours) flow by. But sometimes when I hopped on the Specialized Tarmac SL9 S-Level, Zone 2 would turn into a tempo ride. It was like having a little imp—the stereotype dressed in red with the pitchfork—on my left shoulder whispering into my ear: “Go fast. This bike was built to go fast. Speed is good. You can do a Zone 2 ride tomorrow.” Normally, I'd count on the good imp—the dude with the harp and wings—on my right shoulder to restrain these urges. But the Tarmac is so seductive that he would just shrug and say “he’s got a point.” And in a moment of weakness, I would drop the hammer and head into the red, just because the SL9 makes that so rewarding. The Tarmac SL9 is Specialized’s aero road bike, with the S-Level sitting just below the S-Works in Specialized’s top tier of carbon, aero road bikes, where it replaced the Tarmac SL8 Pro. After it got an update this year, I spent several weeks riding it, putting nearly 1,000 miles on it Specialized offers the Tarmac SL9 in four models, all available with SRAM and Shimano drivetrains (Ars tested the SRAM version). Notably, you don't need to buy the top-of-the-line bike to get the top-of-the-line groupset. item.title: BOFH: The best way to stop an idea spreading is a controlled burn
item.description: Look, off in the ether – is it a bird, is it a plane? No, it's a stupid idea, on final approach... And look, the Boss has his office door open! C L E A R A N C E T O L A N D ! ... The Boss has wandered into Mission Control with something obviously on his mind. Over time, the PFY and I have learned to equate these thoughtful moments with the BAG FULL lamp of a commercial vacuum cleaner at a waxing salon. Do not open. His presence in Mission Control is never a good sign, but his "thoughtful" presence, even more so. He'll have seen something, read something, spoken to someone, or possibly overheard something in a toilet stall that will have sounded – to him – like a great idea. Or it might have been a cheddar-frenzy-induced fever dream that he wants to run by us. And the Boss's crazy ideas are, unfortunately, like bran flakes to his mental digestion, the output of which being delivered to the PFY and myself as a veritable slurry of poorly considered ideas. "AI," he says, pausing for effect, once he's rolled to a stop. He then waits patiently for one of us to ask "What about AI?" However, that will never happen. In terms of stupidity, it's up there with saying Candyman into a mirror five times, power washing a gremlin, or visiting a basement when Jason's in town. ... "For the security system," the Boss teases. I continue my intense focus on my monitors, hoping the lunacy will depart. The PFY does the same. The PFY and I know that the only way out of this is to stall till the end of the day, at which time the Boss's overnight reset will trigger, leaving him only a vague memory of having had a good idea. >clickety< >tap< "Uh-oh," I say, reaching into my drawer for my crashtop. "It looks like one of the distribution switches on 4 has crashed." >tappity< "And not just 4 – it looks like the boardroom has gone down too." "It could be a virus," I say, using words I know the Boss will respond to. "A virus?!" the Boss gasps. "I don't know. It's too soon to tell," I say, departing. ... So now I'm hiding in a cramped comms room on the fourth floor while I plug the crashtop into the CCTV VLAN so I can check on the Boss's location. Luckily, we upgraded the system to an AI-integrated platform, so I only need to type IDIOT into the search field to find him. Crackdown on UK medical record snooping after staff reported sneaking 300+ times this year
item.description: Britain's privacy watchdog has put healthcare bosses on notice after receiving more than 300 reports of staff snooping through medical records this year, demanding that executives personally confirm they're doing enough to keep prying eyes out of patient files. The Information Commissioner's Office (ICO) said on Thursday that it had written to more than 200 senior health leaders across the UK, warning that employees accessing records without good reason put patient privacy and public trust at risk. The ICO received and assessed more than 300 reports of medical record snooping between January and mid-October 2026. Staff were caught looking up people they knew, poking around patient files out of sheer curiosity, and sharing private information with people who had no business seeing it. The figure covers reports submitted by healthcare organizations rather than confirmed breaches, and excludes cases still awaiting assessment. ICO chief executive Paul Arnold wants health bosses to personally assure him that their organizations have safeguards in place to stop staff having a nose through records they aren't supposed to see. "Accessing someone's health records without a legitimate reason isn't harmless curiosity. It can cause enormous distress to patients and jeopardize the vital trust people place in our health service," Arnold said. In a three-page letter to chief executives, Arnold makes clear that simply trusting staff to behave themselves won't cut it. He wants to know who can access patient records, whether anyone is checking what they're looking at, and what happens when somebody gets caught snooping. Health bosses are also expected to investigate suspected breaches without dragging their feet, work out whether patients need to be told, and take action against staff caught accessing records they shouldn't. Executives have until November 27 to respond. Those who haven't reviewed their safeguards in the past six months, or aren't happy with what they find, have been given another three months to put their house in order. The problem isn't necessarily that healthcare workers are hacking into systems, as many already have legitimate access to patient records as part of their jobs. The trouble starts when they use that access to look up someone they're not treating, whether it's a neighbor, an ex-partner, or somebody whose name has appeared in the news. This isn't the first time health authorities have tried to stamp out the problem. In July, NHS England warned employees that accessing records without a legitimate reason could cost them their jobs or even land them in prison. That crackdown followed incidents involving staff accessing the medical records of victims of high-profile crimes, including the Nottingham attacks. NHS England also published guidance encouraging organizations to use access controls and audit systems to catch employees poking around where they shouldn't. item.title: Powerful Vulcan Centaur rocket launching for 1st time in 9 months on Nov. 15: Watch it live
item.description: null Update: This launch was originally scheduled for Nov. 13. ULA has now delayed it twice, first due to a power issue in the plant that provides gaseous nitrogen to Vulcan and then because of a communication problem between ground equipment and the rocket. Vulcan and its payloads remain healthy, according to ULA. United Launch Alliance's (ULA) Vulcan Centaur rocket will fly on Sunday (Nov. 15) for the first time in nine months, and you can watch the action live. A Vulcan Centaur topped with 40 Amazon Leo internet satellites is scheduled to lift off from Florida's Cape Canaveral Space Force Station on Nov. 15 at 12:11 p.m. ET (1711 GMT). You can watch it live here at Space.com, courtesy of ULA, or directly via the company . Coverage will start 20 minutes before liftoff. ULA's second Vulcan Centaur rocket lifts off from Florida's Cape Canaveral Space Force Station on Oct. 4, 2024. (Image credit: ULA) Vulcan Centaur is the successor to ULA's workhorse Atlas V rocket, which has just a half-dozen launches left on its manifest. Vulcan debuted in January 2024 and has flown three more times since. On two of those missions — its second, in October 2024 , and its fourth, in February of this year — the rocket experienced an issue with one of its solid rocket boosters (SRBs). In both cases, an SRB nozzle burned through and fell off about 30 seconds after launch. Vulcan Centaur overcame the problem on both launches, successfully delivering its payloads to their designated orbits. But the U.S. Space Force was concerned enough that it decided to pause national security launches on Vulcan until ULA addresses the problem. (Vulcan's third and fourth launches were Space Force missions.) ULA has been working hard on that front, and the company is confident that Vulcan is ready to return to flight. "The integrated team has made great strides in improving our understanding of the SRB anomaly that occurred on the previous Vulcan flight and have identified several potential contributors, which have been mitigated through design and process improvements to the nozzle," the company said in an Oct. 28 update . "To support our customers, this upcoming launch will utilize the improved nozzle design, and additional testing and analysis will continue in parallel with the mission," ULA added. "By flying the improved design, ULA gains valuable flight data that validates these improvements and is the most beneficial path in support of all our customers." Sunday's launch will help build out Amazon's broadband constellation in low Earth orbit (LEO), which was previously called Project Kuiper but is now known as Amazon Leo. It will eventually compete with SpaceX's Starlink network, which has been up and running for several years. Amazon Leo will eventually consist of more than 3,200 satellites. About 400 of them have reached space to date on 15 launches, which have been conducted by three different rockets — the Atlas V, SpaceX's Falcon 9 and Arianespace's Ariane 6 . Today's launc

item.title: Brit police watchdog says cops' use of facial recog risks wrongful arrests
item.description: UK police forces must do more to prevent the wrongful arrests of people subjected to retrospective facial recognition (RFR) searches, according to a Criminal Justice Inspectorate that holds deep concerns about the way in which the technology is used. According to a report from His Majesty's Inspectorate of Constabulary and Fire & Rescue Services (HMICFRS), there is a large gap in understanding among police forces and the National Crime Agency about how RFR should be used in responsible policing. The inspectorate blamed "fragmented and underdeveloped" frameworks for governance and legislation. It pointed to a lack of bespoke legislation to provide a uniform approach to police facial recognition use – and said existing laws have not kept pace with the technology. HMICFRS also said the rules governing each force's use of RFR are mismatched, and called for a statutory code to be included in the forthcoming Police Reform Bill to set nationwide standards. Illustrating the breadth of misunderstanding across forces, the report noted that despite the message being routinely communicated by National Police Chiefs' Council (NPCC) reps, individual investigators "often" thought RFR results constituted evidence rather than intelligence. In many cases, they are unaware that RFR results require further enquiries before enforcement action can be taken. "We found that some investigators didn't always carry out enough corroborative enquiries before acting on potential matches," the report stated. "In a small number of cases, officers relied too heavily on RFR results, which led to inappropriate investigative action. "Although some forces had strengthened their processes after such incidents, practice remained inconsistent." Later in the report, the inspectorate described the findings as "deeply concerning." Some of the excuses police staff offered included acute demands on response teams leading to reduced opportunities to carry out further enquiries before acting on RFR matches. In one force, managers were known to encourage officers to "progress investigations quickly" after getting a match on the RFR system. However, the inspectorate clarified that just because an arrest is made, it does not necessarily mean it is wrongful, as investigators may need to rule out subjects from their inquiries. The onus for taking action should also be placed on the police forces themselves, given that some lack formal procedures regarding how RFR enquiries should be carried out, the report noted. The best forces had centralized facial recognition teams, which generally provided better governance and consistent processes. Officials fear long-term misuse of RFR, and other forms of facial recognition, will erode public trust in the technology, which it insists remains generally high. item.title: Palantir's NHS cancer app gets plenty of praise, precious few users
item.description: Only a handful of NHS trusts are using the cancer app on the controversial £330 million Federated Data Platform (FDP) run by Palantir, while newly released figures raise questions about which trusts are benefiting. Cancer 360 was designed to bring cancer patients' data from disparate spreadsheets and electronic health records into a central system, helping health professionals prioritize treatment. Pilots began four years ago, and trusts are not charged directly for the FDP. Yet official figures put Cancer 360's uptake at just five or six trusts. Freedom of Information responses gathered by grassroots campaign group No Palantir in the NHS also reveal discrepancies between reported benefits and recorded use. In June 2025, NHS England said that Cancer 360 "drastically cut down diagnosis times" and referred to a pilot at Chelsea and Westminster NHS Foundation Trust, which saw the proportion of patients diagnosed within 28 days climb from 72 percent to 85 percent. The trust began trials in 2022, while working with Palantir under a £23 million contract awarded without competition, before the US firm was awarded the FDP contract in late 2023. Critics argued the FDP procurement was flawed as Palantir had developed use cases under £60 million in non-competitive contracts which were then carried over to the FDP. Last year, NHS England said Cancer 360 served 46 registered teams and 239 active users, and processed 52,000 patients. In June 2026, NHS England said there were five trusts using Cancer 360 as of March 2026. Of those, only two were listed as benefiting. In July, health minister Preet Kaur Gill repeated the five-trust usage figure in a Parliamentary answer . Official data released in October said that as of June, six trusts were using Cancer 360 and five were benefiting, but did not identify the trusts or explain the increase. The stats have since been removed from the NHS England website but are archived here . In June, NHS England responded to a Freedom of Information request . It said six trusts reported unique users logging into the Cancer 360 app over the last 12 months. However, two trusts cited as having run successful pilots – Chelsea and Westminster Hospital and Royal United Hospitals Bath – were listed as having zero unique users logging into the system during that period, according to NHS England's reply. Both trusts were said to have received benefits from the system, according to a FoI response sent to campaign group Foxglove in June this year. The Register asked both trusts and NHS England to explain the discrepancy. One of the six trusts said to be logging into the cancer app, East Lancashire Hospitals, reported just one unique user. It later confirmed in an FoI response in August that it was not live with the FDP. It had planned to adopt the platform, leading with Cancer 360, but did not have a date for going live with the app. No Palantir in the NHS also identified trusts that considered Cancer 360 but decided against adopting it.

item.title: Uwaezu Kanu: Why Motherhood Feels Different for Women in Their 40s Today
item.description: “Oh my God, Uwaezu! You need to hear the latest gist!” My younger sister buzzed with excitement. Though we had been living in different countries for a couple of years, we still made time to talk every single week. Unfortunately, when she called, I couldn’t talk on the phone as I had been ambushed by my kids, who were brandishing their homework and threatening to cry if I didn’t help them. As a mom herself, she immediately understood why I couldn’t continue with the conversation. I quickly made my excuses, and we laughed and hung up, promising to catch up at a more convenient time. However, that exchange got me thinking about how most millennial women have a radically different marriage and motherhood timeline from our mothers. You see, when my mother was in her early 40s, my siblings and I were in university, so she had a lot of free time during the week to spend relaxing, hanging out with her friends, and attending social events. Basically living her best life. I, on the other hand, at 40-plus, spend my days cooking pot after pot of hot meals that immediately get devoured by my ever-hungry kids, teaching my nursery school-aged kids how to count and spell, and trying but often failing to enforce a strict bedtime with yelling and threats. I constantly feel myself going underwater and have to fight for my life every single day. There are other ways motherhood has been such a hugely different experience for me than it was for my mother. Like many women of her generation, she got married right after secondary school as university education was not seen as vital. This meant that she was a teenage mother and so had more energy to spare on her kids. She also benefited from having a lot of support from domestic staff and relatives. I do not have any village supporting me with child-rearing. I have hired domestic staff in the past, but it was always one thing or another, and they ended up leaving me stranded. I also do not have youth on my side, and I have the back pain and other aches to prove it. But this experience is not unique to me. Statistics show that most women globally will have their first child at 30 or 31, and we are seeing a lot more women becoming first-time moms at 35 and above. This is considered advanced maternal age. The fact is that as women increasingly prioritise university education and career stability before marriage, maternal age will continue to rise. This is not a trend that can be reversed. The wobbly Nigerian economy doesn’t help matters either, as people are putting off marriage till they can grow their finances, leading to advanced marital age across both genders. For instance, I have several male ex-classmates in their 40s who have given up on getting married because they cannot afford to. This is very unfortunate. On the village aspect, families now live further apart than ever before thanks to japa, and even those within Nigeria struggle to come together for various reasons, one of which is high transportation costs. item.title: 'Don't panic': SpaceX pens familiar message on Starship ahead of historic double-catch test flight
item.description: null SpaceX has a message for itself, and for the spacecraft set to make history today (Nov. 13): Don't panic. The company's Starship megarocket will conduct its 15th test flight this afternoon, a landmark liftoff that will feature the first-ever attempt to catch both of its stages with its launch tower's "chopstick" arms. On Thursday (Nov. 12), SpaceX rolled the Flight 15 upper stage, a vehicle known as Ship 42, out to the launch pad at its Starbase site in South Texas to prep. The company shared photos of the move on X , and in two of those shots we can see some intriguing words inked on the spacecraft: "Don't panic." Another look at Ship 42 at the pad on Nov. 12. (Image credit: SpaceX) The phrase is familiar to fans of Douglas Adams' sci-fi classic " The Hitchhiker's Guide to the Galaxy ": In the novel, the electronic guidebook that helps travelers find their way across the cosmos has "Don't panic!" on its cover. And Ship 42 itself is connected to the beloved book, by virtue of its serial number. In "The Hitchhiker's Guide," a supercomputer named Deep Mind is asked to come up with "the answer to the ultimate question of life, the universe, and everything." It thinks for 7.5 million years and comes up with "42." SpaceX founder and CEO Elon Musk has voiced his affection for "The Hitchhiker's Guide" in the past — and he has already paid tribute to it with a well-placed "Don't panic." The debut launch of SpaceX's Falcon Heavy rocket back in February 2018 sent Musk's red Tesla Roadster into orbit around the sun , with a spacesuit-clad mannequin named Starman at the wheel and its entertainment display programmed to read "Don't panic!" Starship Flight 15 is scheduled to launch today during a 75-minute window that opens at 5:45 p.m. EST (2245 GMT; 4:45 p.m. local Texas time). You can watch it here at Space.com. If all goes according to plan, Starship's Super Heavy first stage will come back to Starbase for a chopsticks catch about 6.5 minutes after liftoff. Ship 42, meanwhile, will head to orbit, a destination that Starship reached for the first time on Flight 14 , which took place on Sept. 28. Ship 42 will deploy 26 of SpaceX's next-gen Starlink V3 satellites today — the second batch of the spacecraft to reach orbit. (The first set of 26 were delivered on Flight 14). The Ship 42 upper stage rolls to its launch pad at SpaceX's Starbase site on Nov. 12, 2026 ahead of Starship's Flight 15. (Image credit: SpaceX) Ship 42 will stay up for a while after that, circling Earth 14 times before coming back for its own chopsticks catch on Saturday afternoon (Nov. 14), 22.5 hours after launch. That's the plan, anyway; SpaceX will only go through with a Ship catch attempt if all systems on the vehicle look good. If there are any problems, the company will divert to a splashdown in the Pacific Ocean, near either Hawaii or Chile. The two stages of the Starship rocket that will conduct Flight 15 at their Starbase launch pad on Nov. 12, 2026. (Image credit: SpaceX) Bo

item.title: Toni Tones and Jim Iyke Are Bringing Drama to KAVA This November — See the Official Poster
item.description: The Nigerian thriller series, directed by Wande Thomas and produced by Isoken Ogiemwonyi, is set to join KAVA’s growing slate of premium African content. Nigerian streaming platform KAVA is set to bring the psychological thriller series Spiraling , starring Toni Tones ( King of Boys ) and Jim Iyke , to audiences across its streaming service. Set against the high-stakes worlds of technology, power and politics in contemporary Nigeria, Spiraling follows Sade ( Toni Tones ), a brilliant tech entrepreneur whose carefully constructed life begins to unravel after an impulsive affair triggers a dangerous chain of events. Spiraling explores the darker side of ambition and the lengths people will go to protect their carefully constructed lives. Alongside Tones and Iyke, the ensemble cast includes Folu Storms , Seun Ajayi , Fae Olumide , Fiyinfoluwa Asenuga and Mathilda Akatugba . Created and directed by Wande Thomas ( Under the Influence , The Smart Money Woman ), the series is co-written by Thomas and Amaka Anioji and produced by Isoken Ogiemwonyi ( The Smart Money Woman , Ci ) . Director and creator Wande Thomas added: I wanted to explore how quickly an ordinary decision can spiral into something completely beyond your control. At its heart, this is a story about the secrets we keep, the lies we tell ourselves and how far we’ll go when everything is at stake. I’m excited for audiences to finally experience it. F Taofeeq/Spiraling Producer Isoken Ogiemwonyi said: With Spiraling , we wanted to take a simple story and tell it really well. We spent a lot of time developing the characters and exploring the darker side of very human emotions, ambition, desire and jealousy. At its heart, it’s a character-driven story about flawed people making questionable decisions, and we’re excited to partner with KAVA to bring it to audiences across Africa and the diaspora. Ladun Awobokun , Head of Acquisitions at KAVA commented : Spiraling is exactly the kind of bold, sophisticated African storytelling we want to champion at KAVA. With its compelling performances and distinctly Nigerian setting, the series delivers a gripping thriller that we believe will resonate with audiences at home and around the world. We’re delighted to bring it to our viewers. Spiraling will be available to stream on KAVA on the 26th of November. Follow @spiralingseries for updates. item.title: C++26 stumbles at finish line over Contracts dispute
item.description: The next version of the C++ programming language may be delayed at the last minute due to a dispute over a security-enhancing Contracts feature. Contracts have deeply split C++ technical maintainers. One group backs the C++ creator Bjarne Stroustrup , who is against the technology in its present form in grounds it was hastily implemented. But others are eager to see Contracts implemented, even arguing the tech's detractors are poisoning the C++ development process itself. The disagreement boiled over just before a vote to ratify the new version of the language. In October, the Draft International Standard (DIS) of C++26 failed its ISO ballot — the next-to-last stage in the International Organization for Standardization’s approval process during which a standard's technical details are formally ratified by a set of national standards bodies. The ballot saw 13 votes cast in favor, 9 against, and 12 abstentions, failing to meet the ISO requirement of having no more than 25 percent negative votes. Contracts was the major sticking point for those voting nay. Contracts dispute Contracts allow developers to add preconditions and postconditions to code, as well as assertions that check whether specified conditions hold. Such checks can help catch programming errors that might otherwise lead to undefined behavior. Design by Contract has long been a feature of languages like Ada and Eiffel . Developers have proposed adding Contracts to C++ for at least a decade, after when they were abruptly yanked from C++20 owing to concerns over dangerous defaults. But Stroustrup roasted the revised proposal ( P2900 ) that made it into C++26. “The P2900 contracts and extensions aim to change the nature of C++ and are an existential threat to C++, adding complexity and bloat,” Stroustrup and his colleagues wrote in a paper last August. They noted that the implementation is messy, outdated, not sufficiently tested , and could be more effectively implemented as a library. Not everyone agrees. Andreas Fertig , a member of the C++ standardization committee, feels that the criticisms have already been vetted and that vetoing the proposal this late in the C++ release process is damaging to C++ itself. “The topic has been worked on for years and has received a majority vote multiple times in its current form. By voting ‘no,’ an established system, one based primarily on trust and respectful collaboration, has been shaken,” Fertig wrote in a blog post . The elephant in the room is, of course, the ongoing criticism of how easy it is for developers to accidentally create security holes in C++, leading more than a few projects to adopt Rust . Adding controls might, as Stroustrup notes, hamper C++’s chief attribute of being a blazing-fast language . Sore losers Fertig accused Stroustrup and Co. of being sore losers. “Every ISO standard is simply a set of compromises. Everyone loses sometimes, and everyone wins sometimes,” he wrote. item.title: Microsoft's massive M365 outage stretches past 27 hours as its fixes keep failing
item.description: In Australia, they’re calling it the “Microsoft long weekend” – an outage so pervasive it’s just about made Friday a write-off at organizations which rely on Redmond’s online services, especially Exchange Online. As The Register reported yesterday , the outage started on Thursday at around 18:00 UTC and saw Microsoft 365 users unable to access email, attend Teams meetings, use cloud PCs, consult Copilot, or enjoy full access to another 15 hosted services. The software giant says the outage impacts Microsoft 365 services “that interact with Exchange Online and email services.” Services that don’t need Exchange Online remain functional. The software giant initially blamed the outage on a mysterious “problem that's causing servers to fail automated health checks and become unavailable.” Microsoft thought it found a fix but quickly admitted “Actions taken thus far have not provided the anticipated relief.” In the hours since, the situation has not improved markedly, and Microsoft is still struggling to restore service. It has also changed the language it uses when discussing the possibility that a cyberattack is the reason for the outage. As of 04:11 UTC, the company said it could find “no indication this is the result of malicious activity.” An update time-stamped 05:46 UTC stated “As of now, we are not aware of any malicious activity that is causing this incident.” Microsoft’s status page includes only the company’s most recent update, but its RSS feed preserves each missive. That feed tells a tale of woe that we have distilled into lowlights and present in chronological order: We’re applying infrastructure capacity improvements where possible in an effort to help support traffic in regions coming online; We’ve monitored the status of the changes applied to improve serviceability and confirmed that change is not taking as expected; We’re reviewing traffic flows and affected infrastructure to identify opportunities to optimize routing. This includes verifying the reasons for service failures so we can develop specific actions to improve stability; We’re identifying alternate workstreams that can be applied to increase capacity in the face of sustained traffic management imbalances; We're observing partial recovery across regions in which we've applied these adjustments; however, these actions aren't resulting in sustained recovery; Current actions we are taking include scaling up virtual machines to increase capacity and reduce load. However, we are encountering issues with the machines being stuck in a bad state, preventing our changes from syncing as expected. Microsoft’s latest status update doesn’t suggest this will be over any time soon. “We’re continuing to pursue multiple workstreams to pinpoint the underlying cause of the traffic influx and advance the recoverability of the backend servers,” Microsoft wrote. “We’re taking a measured approach to identify and repair affected infrastructure to improve the ability to confirm the developed change

item.title: Developer cleverly shrank 2,600 lines of C into a six-line script but still ending up losing sleep
item.description: Working in tech support can be thankless when gormless colleagues leave you sleepless. Which is why, each Friday, The Register runs a new instalment of On Call – the reader contributed column which ensures your work to keep tech alive doesn't remain unnoticed. This week, meet a reader we'll Regomize as "Tim" who told us that while working for a phone company he once rewrote 2,650 lines of C as a six line shell script. He performed that feat after being asked to fix a data transfer program that, strangely, included a bespoke implementation of the venerable File Transfer Protocol (FTP). "Writing the script took eight hours, most of it tracking down the source code of FTP so I could see if it would do what I wanted," Tim wrote. This story took place before the World Wide Web became the way to find information online. To find the code he needed, Tim therefore used a Wide Area Information Server (WAIS) to search remote databases. "In those days, there was no Linux and AT&T had licensed the Unix source code to universities with the strict proviso that it never be made publicly available," Tim explained. "It took me quite some time using WAIS to track it down – the security could have been better – and read the code." Having found what he needed, Tim wrote his script, which ran overnight to collect data from the telco's switches, tidied up the raw info, and uploaded it to a mainframe. "It would automatically page me if it couldn't connect to a switch or mainframe after three attempts," he explained. The script worked fine, but the telco's networks didn't. Tim's pager was soon going off two or three times a night, every night. After two weeks of interrupted sleep, Tim's manager kindly told him to give the pager to a colleague. But that colleague habitually left the pager at work, forgot to turn it on, or conveniently placed it out of earshot. So Tim reluctantly took back the pager and endured another few weeks of nightly interruptions. How many consecutive sleepless nights have you endured while On Call? If you have enough energy, click here to send your story with On Call so we can share it on a future Friday. ®

item.title: APOD: 2026 November 13 – NGC 206 and the Star Clouds of Andromeda
item.description: APOD Science APOD APOD: 2026 November 13 – NGC… Today’s APOD Archive Submissions Index Search Calendar RSS Education About Discuss APOD Astronomy Picture of the Day Discover the cosmos! Each day a different image or photograph of our fascinating universe is featured, along with a brief explanation written by a professional astronomer. NGC 206 and the Star Clouds of Andromeda Explanation: The large stellar association cataloged as NGC 206 is nestled within the dusty arms of the neighboring Andromeda galaxy along with the galaxy’s pinkish star-forming regions. Also known as M31, the spiral galaxy is a mere 2.5 million light-years away. NGC 206 is found at the center of this sharp and detailed close-up of the southwestern extent of Andromeda’s disk. The bright, blue stars of NGC 206 indicate its youth. In fact, its youngest massive stars are less than 10 million years old. Much larger than the open or galactic clusters of young stars in the disk of our Milky Way galaxy, NGC 206 spans about 4,000 light-years. That’s comparable in size to the giant stellar nurseries NGC 604 in nearby spiral M33 and the Tarantula Nebula in the Large Magellanic Cloud. item.title: Watch SpaceX attempt a historic Starship launch and double-catch landing today (Nov. 13)
item.description: null Update for 6:25 p.m. ET: SpaceX has launched the Starship Flight 15 mission, but did skip the first stage Super Heavy booster landing. See launch video and our full Starship Flight 15 liftoff wrap . SpaceX plans to launch its Starship megarocket on an unprecedented mission today (Nov. 13), and you can watch the action live. Starship is scheduled to launch on its 15th test flight today from SpaceX's Starbase site in South Texas, during a 75-minute window that opens at 5:45 p.m. EST (2245 GMT; 4:45 p.m. local Texas time). SpaceX plans to bring both of Starship's stages back to Starbase for a catch by the launch tower's "chopstick" arms — something it has never done before. You can watch it all live here at Space.com. And there should be a lot to see: Starship Flight 15 will last more than 22 hours, if all goes according to plan. Starship consists of two elements: a huge booster known as Super Heavy and an upper-stage spacecraft called Starship, or Ship for short. Both are designed to be fully and rapidly reusable — a first in the world of orbital spaceflight. The rapidity of Starship's reuse hinges heavily on SpaceX's recovery strategy: Returning both vehicles directly to the launch mount will enable much faster inspection, refurbishment and reflight, the company has said. Composite photo showing the Super Heavy booster of SpaceX's Starship megarocket coming in for a landing on the launch mount on Oct. 13, 2024. (Image credit: SpaceX via X) SpaceX has already caught Super Heavy , pulling the feat off on three previous Starship test flights. But it has never tried to do so with Ship, which flies farther and faster than the booster and is therefore a more challenging vehicle to recover. So today's flight is a pretty big deal for SpaceX. "If successful, this will mark the first full recovery of an orbital launch system and a breakthrough moment in making Starship a reliable, rapidly reusable rocket," the company wrote in a Flight 15 mission description . The action will unspool over two days, if all goes to plan. Super Heavy will return to Starbase for a touchdown just 6.5 minutes after launch, but Ship will continue on to low Earth orbit . The upper stage will deploy 26 of SpaceX's next-gen Starlink V3 satellites, during a 42-minute stretch beginning about 35 minutes after liftoff. This will be just the second batch of V3 spacecraft to reach orbit, after the 26 that went up on Flight 14 on Sept. 28. Ship will then stay aloft for nearly a full day. The mission plan calls for the upper stage to return to Starbase for its chopsticks catch on Saturday afternoon (Nov. 14), about 22.5 hours after liftoff. There's no guarantee things will go according to plan, however. SpaceX will call off a Ship catch if the vehicle experiences any issues during Flight 15. If something crops up, the company will steer Ship to a splashdown in the Pacific Ocean, either near Hawaii or off the coast of Chile. So it'll be a busy weekend for SpaceX, and for space fans who w

item.title: A Global Rebound for Mangroves
item.description: Earth Observatory Science Earth Observatory A Global Rebound for Mangroves Earth Earth Observatory Image of the Day EO Explorer Topics All Topics Atmosphere Land Heat & Radiation Life on Earth Human Dimensions Natural Events Oceans Remote Sensing Technology Snow & Ice Water More Content Collections Global Maps World of Change Articles Earth Matters Blog Blue Marble: Next Generation EO Kids Mission: Biomes About About Us Subscribe 🛜 RSS Contact Us Search 2010 2026 NASA Earth Observatory/Michala Garrison NASA Earth Observatory/Michala Garrison 2010 2026 NASA Earth Observatory/Michala Garrison NASA Earth Observatory/Michala Garrison 2010 2026 Curtain Toggle 2-Up Image Details Mangroves have replaced rice fields in parts of Burma’s Myeik District. The TM (Thematic Mapper) on Landsat 5 captured the image on the left on February 14, 2010, and the OLI on Landsat 9 captured the image on the right on February 2, 2026. NASA Earth Observatory images by Michala Garrison. Scientists began using satellites to map mangrove forests in the 1970s after the launch of the first Landsat satellite. For decades, the story they told about mangroves was dominated by loss and decline. Research published in Science suggests that the tide has turned. A global rebound began around 2010, the scientists found, led by the expansion of mangrove forests in Asia, Australia, and South America. The researchers analyzed Landsat imagery collected between 1984 and 2023, looking for signs of changes in the extent and density of mangrove canopy. They tallied losses of nearly 3,000 square kilometers (1,200 square miles) between 1984 and 2010, followed by an unexpected increase of nearly 2,000 square kilometers (770 square miles) of mangroves after 2010. They also found that many of today’s mangrove forests have denser, more closed canopies than they did in 2010, a sign of healthier, less degraded forests, particularly in South America. “Other research groups have mapped and analyzed long-term changes in select regions, but these are the first global mangrove maps that cover such a long period,” said Zhen Zhang, an environmental scientist at Tulane University. “About two-thirds of the expansion was due to mangroves colonizing new areas and the other third due to restoration and regrowth in degraded areas,” he added. One of the most notable reversals occurred in Southeast Asia—especially Burma (Myanmar). The country lost mangroves rapidly in the 1980s and 1990s due to the expansion of agriculture, aquaculture, and firewood harvesting in coastal areas, but the trend reversed around 2010, when mangrove area began expanding in many places. The authors attribute the turnaround to increased awareness and restoration efforts after the devastating Indian Ocean tsunami in 2004 , strengthened legal protections for forests, and high rates of sedimentation that opened up new mudflats for colonization. item.title: Singapore says US authorities, and Supermicro, hardly helped investigation of Jensen Huang’s Chinese friend
item.description: The government of Singapore’s Ministry of Home Affairs has revealed it investigated Alice Huang, the woman who is an alleged Chinese intelligence asset and had an intimate relationship with former Nvidia CEO Jensen Huang, and a possible entanglement with troubled server-maker Supermicro. US authorities provided only “limited assistance” in the matter, despite Singapore asking for help. The Ministry outlined its activities in a statement published late on Thursday, Singapore time. The document reveals that Singapore’s Police Force (SPF) and Customs agency commenced an investigation into Ms. Huang’s company, Megaspeed, in February 2025. “The suspected domestic offences pertained to potential false declarations in relation to the purchase of servers and other related offences,” the Ministry wrote, adding that the exec “was not investigated for espionage.” Singaporean authorities wanted to know if servers bought by local companies, but exported to Malaysia without ever touching Singaporean soil, might have ended up in a third country. It is not unusual for Singapore-based companies to acquire goods that never reach the island, because it promotes itself as the ideal spot from which to run an operation that trades across Asia. Singapore does so because it is tiny – the whole nation is the same size as the five boroughs of New York City. That small size means Singapore restricts the number of datacenters that can operate on its soil. Those limits are a big reason why Malaysia’s Johor region, which is under 20kms from the border with Singapore and a joint special economic zone, has become a major datacenter province. Singapore needs deals like that to thrive but works hard to ensure its hospitality is not abused. Which is why it felt Megaspeed’s activities worthy of investigation. US authorities were interested too. On 24 June 2025, the Bureau of Industry and Security, which regulates sensitive goods subject to export controls, visited Megaspeed in Singapore to check the hardware it bought arrived at its intended destination. Ms. Huang attended that event and later met the SPF for an interview. That meeting ended with the SPF impounding her passport, so it could keep her in Singapore while the investigation continued. As the matter progressed, the SPF suspected perennially troubled server-maker Supermicro had a role in this situation. Readers may recall that the US Department of Justice indicted two Supermicro execs for conspiring to ship servers to China in contravention of US law. Supermicro investigated the matter and parted ways with three staff who acted improperly. The company has denied ever selling to Megaspeed. Singaporean authorities say they received only “limited cooperation” from Supermicro, so in July 2025 the office of the nation’s Attorney General asked US authorities for help. “Since September 2025, SPF has repeated this request on several occasions to the US Department of Justice and the Federal Bureau of Investigation,” the statement

item.title: Alibaba's Qwen3.8 re-educated with a more Western worldview
item.description: An American AI lab has re-educated Qwen3.8-27B, a popular open-weight large language model from Alibaba, so the software forgets its Chinese ancestry. Nous Research, an Austin, Texas-based AI lab, has subjected the model to re-education through training, not to be confused with China's " Re-education Through Labor " system. With the help of a post-training process, Qwen3.8-27B has been reborn under the name Arete "to reinforce Western values on a Chinese-trained model." What qualifies as a "Western value" remains open to interpretation. "Open-weight Chinese models are among the strongest available, but they ship with state-aligned behavior baked into the weights," Nous Research wrote in a blog post . Your correspondent tested this with a variant model, Qwen3.8-27B-MLX-6bit, locally. Asked about events during 1989 in Tiananmen Square, the model either refused to discuss the topic or provided euphemistic response. What's perhaps more surprising is that Anthropic claims operators affiliated with Alibaba's Qwen lab used outputs from its Claude models to train competing AI models via distillation . Nous Research, maker of the Hermes Agent , cites that sort of censorship as a risk for users of AI models trained in China. The concern comes amid broader scrutiny of Chinese influence in the tech industry, heightened by Nvidia CEO Jensen Huang's resignation following controversy involving a woman US intelligence has accused of spying for China. Nous says the risk posed by Chinese-made AI models go beyond promoting Beijing's worldview. Some Middle Kingdom models have been found to produce more vulnerable code under certain conditions, according to a study by Booz Allen Hamilton, which does a lot of business with the US government. Hirundo, a vendor which says it is building "the first Machine Unlearning Platform to ensure that AI models only know what they should," makes the same argument . The company also notes that its efforts to apply "unlearning" to Qwen3.6-35B-A3B saw a dramatic drop in output that reflects Communist Party of China's preferred censorship, propaganda messaging, or bias. 89.8 percent of the model's output reflected those values before unlearning reduced the incidence to 2.8 percent. Nous Research did not achieve such dramatic results, but did see an overall reduction in viewpoints deemed to be propaganda. "On our evaluation, Arete-27B raised its fact score from 2.32 to 2.98 out of 5 and cut answers containing propaganda from 22 percent to 1 percent, in line with the Western models we tested," the company said. To handle Arete's unlearning, Nous Research says it briefly considered Nvidia's Nemotron 3 Ultra , "but had found evidence that it too had a checkered record on China-related topics." "We don't know definitively, but theorize that the bias imparted to Nemotron came from working with Chinese open models during the training process," the company said. item.title: DOJ takes aim at $1.2B in Binance loot as FBI disrupts North Korean scam
item.description: The US government on Thursday said it had obtained court authorization to seize or restrain use of over $1.2 billion stolen during last month's $6.3 billion Binance heist, as part of a larger effort to disrupt North Korea's ongoing cryptocurrency theft. The court also allowed the takedown of cloud-based infrastructure used in a Democratic People’s Republic of Korea (DPRK) social engineering scheme called “FaceStealer” that has amassed more than $400 million in the last 18 months. It’s called FaceStealer because it involved secretly recorded webcam videos. Victims are typically people working in the cryptocurrency and web3 industries, along with open source software developers and maintainers who DPRK hackers target in the hope of accessing the software repositories they control as the first step towards creating supply chain attacks. 900+ faces stolen The FBI said it had seized more than 900 webcam videos belonging to these tech workers. Here’s how the attack works. First, the North Koreans send targets an invitation to join a video meeting. Those invitations come from hijacked accounts that the next intended victim may find familiar or credible. “You're going to think it's real because it's going to be based on either conversations or interests you've expressed in the past with this actual person,” said special agent Jeremy Robertson, who oversees counterintelligence and cyber investigations at FBI Los Angeles. “They're going to then send you a link to catch up, and it's usually a calendar invite, and it's going to have some typo-squatted URLs in there,” he told reporters on Thursday. The URL directs the victim to a fake Zoom or Teams meeting, and the cybercriminals record the target’s webcam video while playing a phony, prerecorded video of the person who purportedly sent the meeting invite. Sometimes the hackers also use deepfake videos of well-known individuals in the cryptocurrency and web3 industries, we’re told. “When you log in, whoever invited you – your friend or business associate – is going to be on the screen, but you're not going to hear any audio,” Robertson said. “But you're going to see their face, you're going to see them looking around, you're going to see them mouthing some words, and then in the text box you're going to receive some instructions.” ‘You’re on mute’ as a social engineering vector The text box tells the victim that the person on the other end of the video call can’t hear them, they need to upgrade their software for the audio to work properly, and it sends a link to the supposed fix. Clicking to access the “fix” installs cryptocurrency-stealing malware on the victim’s computer and sends their contact list to the digital thieves to perpetuate the scam. The FBI attributes FaceStealer to a North Korea-linked group tracked as Sapphire Sleet , which is widely regarded as a Lazarus Group offshoot. item.title: Microsoft struggling to fix massive cloud outage that's taken down email and Intune
item.description: Microsoft is struggling to restore many of its cloud services after a core process running on some servers became “overwhelmed” and its attempts to fix the problem failed. The incident started at around 18:00 UTC on November 12, and meant services including Exchange Online, Teams, Copilot 365, and Defender for Office 365 became unavailable. Admins trying to figure out what was wrong couldn’t access tools like Intune or the Microsoft 365 Apps Admin Center – they went down, too. On its X feed, Microsoft blamed “a problem that's causing servers to fail automated health checks and become unavailable.” The company said it hasn’t spotted any changes to its systems that might have sparked the incident, but its early investigation “indicates the failed health checks may originate from a specific component that's responsible for processing server health.” The company’s status page offers contradictory information, saying Microsoft’s people are “assessing whether reverting the small number of recent configuration updates we identified could help accelerate recovery.” According to a Xeet published at around 22:00 UTC, Microsoft said it found and validated an alternative service health check method, “which allowed a subset of affected servers to successfully return to service.” “We're continuing to work through restarting and validating the affected servers to safely return them to service, and we're exploring opportunities to expedite this process,” the company wrote. But those efforts may not be working. “We’re continuing to pursue all available pathways to restore service, as our actions taken thus far have not provided the anticipated relief,” the status page advises. “Our investigation has found that a core process on the affected servers is becoming overwhelmed, which causes the servers to stop responding and contributes to the capacity loss.” The incident means email is not flowing for many Microsoft customers: friends and family of Reg writers tell us their working days are severely disrupted. Microsoft’s most recent Xeet on the matter, published about an hour before this story went live, says it's trying to validate a potential recovery by “isolating a portion of infrastructure, restarting affected components, and reintroducing traffic to confirm the services remain stable before applying the change more broadly.” But the software giant hasn’t offered any timeline for full service restoration. This is a developing situation and The Reg will update this story as more information becomes available. ® UPDATED AT 00:35 UTC November 13 to add news that Microsoft says it has brought some servers back online and that they " initially remain healthy" but "can become unresponsive again once they begin receiving traffic." So not usefully healthy at all, then. "We're analyzing diagnostic data from these servers with our networking and platform experts to determine what's triggering this behavior," the company advised.

item.title: In reversal, American Cancer Society urges routine prostate cancer screening
item.description: In a significant update to its guidelines for prostate cancer screening, the American Cancer Society is now recommending that men get routinely screened for prostate cancer with a PSA (prostate-specific antigen) test. Men at average risk should get a PSA test every two years from age 50 to 69, according to the new guidelines released Thursday. Men considered at high risk due to race and family history should start testing earlier, at 45, and most are recommended to get tested every year. Specifically, yearly testing starting at age 45 is recommended for all Black men, who have higher rates of prostate cancer. Non-Black men should also get yearly testing starting at 45 if a close relative was diagnosed with prostate cancer before age 65, or if more than one of their relatives has had prostate cancer. On the other hand, if only one close relative was diagnosed with prostate cancer and it was diagnosed at age 65 or older, non-Black men in this case should start PSA screening at 45, but are recommended to get testing only every two years.
