item.title: The Francophone African Music Industries Fair (SIMA) announces its 3rd Edition in Republic of Benin | November 12th – 13th
item.description: The Francophone African Music Industries Fair (SIMA) announces the third edition of the event, taking place on November 12–13, 2026, in Cotonou, Republic of Benin. Following its previous edition, which brought together more than 6,700 participants and over 3,000 industry professionals, this pan-African gathering dedicated to the cultural and creative industries returns with a clear ambition: African Music: From the Stage to Global Influence. SIMA 2026 is supported by major institutional and private-sector partners, including the Ministry of Culture, Arts and Heritage of Benin,the Ministry of Tourism and Foreign Trade of Benin,the Embassy of France in Côte d’Ivoire,the BOAD Foundation, as well as SACEM, Sony Music and Warner Music Africa. These partnerships reflect the growing interest in the development and structuring of Africa’s cultural and creative industries. For the second consecutive year, Benin will host SIMA, in line with the country’s broader efforts to strengthen the role of the cultural and creative industries in the structural transformation of its economy and to enhance its cultural influence at both regional and international levels. Co-founded in 2022 by cultural entrepreneur Mamby Diomandé and artist and producer Pit Baccardi , SIMA has established itself as a platform dedicated to structuring, connecting and developing Africa’s creative ecosystems. By placing music at the heart of a broader reflection on the transformation of culture and the creative industries, SIMA also seeks to address the technological shifts reshaping the sector—from artificial intelligence to new ways of creating, distributing and consuming content. At a time when Africa’s creative economy could generate up to 20 million jobs by 2030, the 2026 edition aims to take a further step forward by contributing to the positioning of African creativity as a powerful driver of soft power, value creation and international influence. “African music is no longer simply a cultural phenomenon: it has become a force of influence. Our challenge now is to transform this influence into sustainable economic power. SIMA aims to build connections between creators, investors, institutions and markets so that the international visibility of our talents translates into measurable data, content monetization, economic opportunities, jobs and value creation for the continent.” Mamby Diomandé , Co-Founder of SIMA Three Priorities for Turning Creativity into Economic Power To address the challenges of a rapidly evolving global market, SIMA 2026 will structure its programme around three key priorities. The first focuses on competitiveness and internationalization, with the aim of strengthening the economic performance of industry stakeholders and facilitating the international export of African talent. item.title: Ayra Starr Joins Coachella 2027 Lineup Alongside SZA, Dua Lipa & More
item.description: Ayra Starr returns with her third studio album, Starrgirl. Ayra Starr is taking her global run to another big stage! The Nigerian singer has been named among the performers at Coachella 2027, adding another major festival appearance to her growing list of international milestones. The Beninese-born singer, who rose to prominence as one of Afrobeats’ leading voices after joining Mavin Records, is set to perform on both weekends of the festival, Sunday, April 11, and Sunday, April 18, 2027. Coachella will take place at the Empire Polo Club in Indio, California. It’s been a big year for Ayra, with her third studio album, Starrgirl, adding to an already exciting run. Fans heading to the festival can look forward to hearing songs from the project, including “ Tornado ” and “ Midnight in New York “, as well as her collaboration “ Gimme Dat “. There’s also room for crowd favourites such as “ Rush “, “ Commas ” and “ Heaven Baby “. Ayra shares the Sunday bill with headliner SZA , alongside Victoria Monét , Jorja Smith , Becky G and Don Toliver . The wider festival, running from April 9 to 11 and April 16 to 18, will also feature headliners Dua Lipa and Tame Impala , with Madonna set for a special appearance in the dance tent. Her Coachella booking follows another major moment in London, where she performed at Tottenham Hotspur Stadium as part of the NFL International Games halftime show, becoming the first African artist to headline the show. And there’s even more for fans to look forward to. Ayra has announced her 20-city Starrgirl World Tour , which will take her across Europe and North America in early 2027 before she heads to the California desert for Coachella. What a year ahead for the Starr girl. The official Coachella 2027 lineup featuring Nigerian singer Ayra Starr alongside headliners Dua Lipa, Tame Impala, and SZA at the Empire Polo Club in Indio, California. item.title: Did comets bring building blocks of life to Earth? Scientists aren't so sure anymore
item.description: The origin of life on Earth remains a mystery. New research shows that comets almost certainly did not bring the chemical building blocks of life to our planet. Life as we know it is based around carbon chemistry, also known as organic chemistry. Complex organic molecules are the fundamental building blocks of biochemical compounds such as nucleobases, amino acids, sugars and so on that act as the machinery for biochemistry on Earth . Two big questions are where did this complex chemistry originate? Did these complex organic molecules form on Earth, or were they delivered here from space? New research led by planetary scientist Richard Anslow of the Institute for Astronomy at the University of Cambridge has now seemingly ruled out comets as the origin of complex organic molecules on Earth. "Historically, scientists thought that comets were important for the origin of life on Earth, because they carried carbon and nitrogen-bearing molecules, so these giant space snowballs were almost like a 'get-out-of-jail-free card' that brought all the molecules a planet would need to seed life," said Anslow in a statement . Stripping the romance from the Earth's turbulent past Comet impacts on Earth were much more frequent in the first half-billion years of the solar system ’s existence, when there were still lots of debris leftover from the formation of the planets. For over a century comet impacts had been considered a prime suspect in the search for what brought the building blocks of life to Earth. However, while comets bringing the building blocks of life to Earth is "kind of a romantic idea," according to Anslow, the University of Cambridge researcher added that the team's results suggest that is highly unlikely. Anslow and colleagues arrived at this conclusion based upon computer modeling by using the very latest simulations depicting the origin and evolution of comets and their orbits, their interactions with Earth's atmosphere as they enter it, and of the hypervelocity comet impacts themselves. In particular, they used the fate of hydrogen cyanide as a proxy for what happens to complex organic molecules in comet impacts. Hydrogen cyanide is frequently found in comets and was even detected in the interstellar comet 3I/ATLAS . An artist’s impression of a comet crashing into the early Earth (Image credit: Scarlett White) The problem is that comets are generally moving at too great a velocity. For organic molecules to survive impact, the impact velocity would have to be below 33,500 miles per hour (15 kilometers per second). Anslow and his colleagues found that, in general, comets travel too fast and enter Earth’s atmosphere at too sharp an angle for complex organic molecules to survive. Instead, they are mostly vaporized on impact. Even on the rare occasions that the complex organic molecules survived, they were usually not in great enough abundance to provide any meaningful prebiotic chemistry. item.title: 'There's tremendous demand': Rocket Lab raises price of Neutron launch from $55 million to $70 million
item.description: null The coming launch bottleneck has ramped up demand for a rocket that has yet to leave the ground. Rocket Lab announced on Monday (Nov. 9) that it recently raised the price of a Neutron launch from $55 million to $70 million — an increase of more than 25%, for a ride on a rocket that's set to debut in 2027. "Launch is extremely constrained, and that is exactly the situation we predicted," Rocket Lab founder and CEO Peter Beck said on Monday during the company's third-quarter earnings call. "We saw a pent-up launch market on the horizon, and rather than provide early discounted launches, we set out to deliver a rocket into an environment with extreme demand at full price or higher." Rocket Lab is best known for Electron , a workhorse small-satellite launcher that debuted in 2017 and now has 90 orbital missions under its belt. The 59-foot-tall (18 meters) expendable rocket and can haul 660 pounds (300 kilograms) to low Earth orbit (LEO). Neutron is the company's entry into the medium-lift market. It features a reusable first stage, stands 141 feet (43 m) tall and can carry 14.3 tons (13 metric tons) of payload to LEO. Rocket Lab announced Neutron back in 2021 and first targeted a 2024 debut for the vehicle. But various problems have cropped up over the years, pushing things back. Last month, for example, Rocket Lab announced that it was delaying the first Neutron flight from late 2026 into 2027 due to a manufacturing issue (which it says is now under control). Such setbacks have not dampened demand for Neutron's services, however. During Monday's call, Beck revealed that Rocket Lab booked eight Neutron launches during the third quarter of 2026, which ran from July 1 through Sept. 30. The contracts for those eight flights are worth "a total of roughly 515 million, including multiple missions on a new escalated base price of $70 million," Beck said. Neutron's first 16 launches are now sold out, he added, and bookings from here on will be for flights in the 2030s. "The demand is a function of both a tightening global launch supply and our customers' confidence that Rocket Lab is the right partner to break the world's launch bottleneck," Beck said. Artist's illustration of Neutron's first stage coming down for a landing on a ship at sea. (Image credit: Rocket Lab) That bottleneck is coming in 2028 or so, when SpaceX plans to retire its Falcon 9 rocket . For some perspective, and comparison with Neutron: SpaceX currently charges $74 million for each Falcon 9 launch. The rocket has a reusable first stage and can carry about 25 tons (22.7 metric tons) to LEO. The medium lifter has been the world's most prolific rocket for the past few years. In 2025, for example, it flew 165 times — roughly the same number of orbital missions as all other launchers in the world combined. And all 165 of those flights were successful. item.title: Omotunde’s 5 Days in South Korea: Exploring LG’s World of Innovation & Discovering the Best of Korean Culture
item.description: Hello BNers, Omotunde here. item.title: Hubble Space Telescope reveals glittering stars with mysterious origins | Space photo of the day for Nov. 11, 2026
item.description: null The Hubble Space Telescope has captured a breathtaking view of thousands of stars glittering like cosmic jewels in a dazzling display of blue, gold and orange. But this spectacular scene is far more than just a pretty picture. Some of these stars are almost as old as the universe itself and could hold clues to how our Milky Way formed. M30 is a globular star cluster located approximately 27,500 light-years from Earth. (Image credit: ESA/Hubble & NASA, M. Libralato, G. Piotto, A. Sarajedini) What is it? The exquisite image released by ESA on Nov. 5 shows Messier 30 (M30), a densely packed collection of stars located approximately 27,500 light-years from Earth in the constellation Capricornus. M30 is a globular cluster, a roughly spherical collection of tens of thousands to millions of stars held together by gravity . Our Milky Way is home to at least 150 of these ancient stellar gatherings, some of which are estimated to be between 11.5 billion and 13.5 billion years old. For comparison, the universe itself is approximately 13.8 billion years old! Why is it amazing Besides looking like a vast cosmic treasure trove glittering across the universe, M30 also has a fascinating story to tell. Globular clusters are essentially cosmic time capsules. Their ancient stars preserve chemical clues about the conditions that existed when they formed, helping astronomers piece together the Milky Way's early history. Astronomers have also discovered that M30, along with several other globular clusters, traverses the Milky Way in the opposite direction to the galaxy's rotation. This unusual motion raises the intriguing possibility that M30 may not have formed in our galaxy at all. It could have simply been captured by the Milky Way billions of years ago.

item.title: Why I recommend the Seestar S30 Plus smart telescope for beginners — full review
item.description: null I’ve used several smart telescopes over the last few years, but I'd recommend the ZWO Seestar S30 Plus to almost anyone wanting to get started in astrophotography. At $499/€499, it’s a complete imaging system that can photograph galaxies, nebulae and star clusters automatically, even from a light-polluted city. Better still, it’s so small that it can live on a bookshelf. The Pleiades (M45), photographed in mosaic mode with the Seestar S30 Plus. (Image credit: Jamie Carter) Jamie Carter The Andromeda Galaxy (M31) photographed using the Seestar S30 Plus. (Image credit: Jamie Carter) Jamie Carter The Dumbbell Nebula (M27) photographed using the Seestar S30 Plus. (Image credit: Jamie Carter) Jamie Carter I recently captured images of the Dumbbell Nebula (M27), the North America Nebula (NGC 7000), the Andromeda Galaxy (M31) and the Pleiades (M45) with the S30 Plus. All were remarkably easy to capture, and none of the images accompanying this review required external processing. It’s basically point-and-shoot astrophotography — if you live under light-polluted skies, that’s a game-changer. Star trails photographed using the Seestar S30 Plus’s dedicated Star Trail mode. (Image credit: Jamie Carter) (Image credit: Jamie Carter) I also think the S30 Plus makes an ideal companion to a conventional optical telescope. I can set it to photograph a nebula I have no hope of seeing under light pollution while I try to find brighter objects through the eyepiece of another telescope. It will then get on with collecting photons while I enjoy observing. For anyone who already owns a telescope but doesn’t want the expense and complexity of conventional astrophotography, that’s a compelling proposition. I photographed nebulas despite light pollution The S30 Plus is Seestar’s new entry-level smart telescope. (Image credit: Jamie Carter) (Image credit: Jamie Carter) One problem with buying a cheap optical telescope is that deep-sky objects rarely resemble the colorful photographs you see online. The moon, planets and bright star clusters can look wonderful through an eyepiece, but faint galaxies and nebulas are much harder to appreciate, particularly from a town or city. Like all smart telescopes, the S30 Plus gets around that problem by photographing objects rather than showing them directly. Its camera takes repeated exposures, which the telescope automatically stacks to reduce noise and gradually reveal faint detail. The longer you leave it working, the better the resulting image tends to become. Being able to photograph colorful nebulas without traveling to a remote observing site is one of the biggest attractions of the S30 Plus. For beginners living in cities, it could transform their experience of astronomy. It’s the perfect companion to my optical telescope The North America Nebula (NGC 7000) photographed using the Seestar S30 Plus. item.title: NASA's new UVEX space telescope will peer deep into the universe's most violent events
item.description: null A new NASA space telescope will study the universe in ultraviolet light to reveal the violent and turbulent events that bubble under what appears to be a cosmic sea of tranquility. The Ultraviolet Explorer (UVEX) mission, developed by NASA in conjunction with the California Institute of Technology (Caltech), will be the first mission to create deep all-sky maps in ultraviolet light. Thus, when it launches in 2031, UVEX will join new sky-mapping surveys like NASA's SPHEREx (Spectro-Photometer for the History of the Universe, Epoch of Reionization and Ices Explorer), which scans the cosmos in infrared, and the Vera C. Rubin Observatory, which does the same over the southern hemisphere in visible light, in creating deep-sky maps across a broad swathe of the electromagnetic spectrum. UVEX's ultraviolet views will reveal explosive events such as the collisions between ultra-dense stellar corpses called neutron stars and the supernova explosions that mark the deaths of massive stars and the births of neutron stars and black holes. Additionally, the NASA ultraviolet telescope should be able to detect a multitude of low-mass galaxies much closer to the Milky Way than similar galaxies that are currently being observed millions and even billions of light-years away by NASA's James Webb Space Telescope (JWST) . The $590 million UVEX mission will "advance fundamental frontiers in astrophysics, from understanding the smallest galaxies to diagnosing the aftermath of neutron-star mergers and other cosmic explosions," the mission's principal investigator, Caltech physics professor Fiona Harrison, said in an Oct. 27 statement . "The first major ultraviolet space mission in two decades, UVEX is a bold leap forward in our exploration of the ultraviolet universe," Caltech President Ray Jayawardhana said in the same statement. UVEX will paint a picture of cosmic life, death and afterlife UVEX will benefit from a major leap forward in UV sensitivity thanks to its Caltech-built sensors, which are based on complementary metal–oxide–semiconductor (CMOS) imaging technology. This will help the spacecraft tap into what Harrison described as "the untapped opportunity in the UV." UVEX will be uniquely poised to spot millions of nearby, small, and faint galaxies that are teeming with infant stars that emit bright UV light. "In optical light, it's very hard to distinguish these nearby galaxies from faraway ones that look similar," Harrison said. "UV light will make them easier to find." UVEX won't just be investigating the infancy of stars , however. It will also examine the deaths of ancient stars in the form of supernovas. The supernova relic Pa 30, as seen by the Gemini north telescope. (Image credit: International Gemini Observatory/NOIRLab/NSF/AURA) Supernovas occur when a massive star runs out of fuel for nuclear fusion and can no longer support itself against the inward push of its own gravity. As the core of the star collapses, its outer layers are blasted outward

item.title: Meagan Good & Jonathan Majors Look Picture-Perfect at AFRIFF in Lagos
item.description: Meagan Good and Jonathan Majors coordinating in neutral tones and a red cap accent for AFRIFF. Who knew an ivory mini dress and a classic black suit could make such an interesting pairing? During their time in Lagos for AFRIFF, Meagan Good and Jonathan Majors posed for a studio portrait in two looks that took very different approaches to dressing up. Meagan’s dress brought together colourful beadwork, a fitted silhouette and a floor-length train, while Jonathan opted for black tailoring, an open-neck white shirt and a red cap. And while his outfit keeps things relatively simple, there’s nothing ordinary about the details of hers. Let’s start with Meagan’s dress, because there is quite a lot happening here. At first glance, the ivory mini might seem relatively simple, but look a little closer and the details begin to unfold. The fitted halter-neck bodice is covered in rows of turquoise, bronze and dark green beads, arranged horizontally to follow the shape of her waist. Then there’s the skirt, which takes a more unexpected turn with clusters of dark beaded embellishments scattered across the fabric. And just when you think you’ve taken it all in, an extended panel falls from the side of the mini skirt, creating a long, floor-sweeping train. It’s a fun combination of short and dramatic, with the beadwork giving the dress plenty to say without needing much else. Meagan Good styled in a sculpted halter-neck corset dress featuring multi-coloured beaded detailing and a side train. Meagan kept the rest of her styling fairly simple. Black ankle-strap heels and a textured black clutch were her accessories of choice, while her voluminous curls were left loose around her shoulders. Her bronze-toned makeup and glossy nude lip tied everything together without competing with the dress. Jonathan went in a completely different direction, keeping things classic with a black jacket and matching trousers over a white shirt, worn open at the neck. A grey patterned scarf added another detail around the collar, while his light-framed sunglasses and black patent shoes completed the outfit. But it’s the red cap that really changes the look. Against all that black and white, it gives the outfit a welcome hit of colour and makes the styling feel more personal. Meagan Good and Jonathan Majors showcasing intricate beaded dress embroidery and red cap styling. It’s an interesting pairing: Meagan’s dress has all the beadwork, colour and movement, while Jonathan’s outfit is built around simple tailoring and a few well-chosen accessories. There’s plenty to appreciate in both, wouldn’t you agree? Meagan Good displaying horizontal beadwork in turquoise and bronze paired with bronze-toned makeup. *** Photo Credit: Amplify Africa/Instagram The post Meagan Good & Jonathan Majors Look Picture-Perfect at AFRIFF in Lagos appeared first on BellaNaija - Showcasing Africa to the world. item.title: What Are The Effective Ways of Using AI?
item.description: Two people engaging with technology in a contemporary hotel lobby work setting. Artificial Intelligence (AI) is changing how people learn, work, communicate and solve problems. In today’s world, if you’re not on board with AI, it could be said you’re being resistant to the fastest-growing technological innovation in the world. From students researching academic subjects to professionals developing business ideas, AI tools have become companions in everyday activities for people. They can help save time, explore new ideas, understand difficult concepts and approach tasks differently. However, as more people embrace these AI tools, it is important to understand that using AI effectively goes beyond knowing what prompts to enter. It requires knowing when to use it, how to question its responses and, most importantly, when to rely on your own knowledge and judgement. AI could make us better at what we do, not make us dependent on it. Here are ways we think you use AI effectively: Use AI as a Research Assistant One of the most effective ways to use AI is for research and information gathering. Whether you are writing an article, preparing a presentation or exploring an unfamiliar subject, AI can help you identify relevant topics, explain complex ideas and suggest areas worth investigating. You can ask it to break down unfamiliar concepts, identify key questions, or suggest research directions. However, do not treat every response as fact. Verify important information using credible sources, published research, books and reliable websites. AI can help you find information, but you are responsible for establishing what is true. Use AI to Brainstorm and Explore Ideas Like knowledge gathering, AI can brainstorm ideas with you. Sometimes, the hardest part of starting a project is knowing where to begin. AI can help you overcome this challenge by suggesting ideas, exploring different approaches and presenting perspectives you may not have considered. For writers, entrepreneurs, researchers and creatives, it can be a useful brainstorming partner. You can share an idea, ask questions about its strengths and weaknesses, and explore ways to develop it. However, brainstorming should not become an excuse to surrender your imagination. Let AI expand your thinking, not replace it. Use AI to Improve Your Work, Not Replace Your Skills This is becoming more important. AI can help you identify grammatical errors, improve sentence construction, organise information, summarise lengthy documents and make your communication clearer. It can reduce the time spent on repetitive tasks and create more room for important responsibilities. The important thing is that you should remain actively involved. Read what AI produces, question its suggestions and make the final decisions yourself. Your skills improve when you practise them, not when you consistently hand them over to a machine. item.title: From Lagos to Cotonou! BN’s Osas is Taking You Inside SIMA 2026
item.description: One thing you can always bet on, as far as BellaNaija is concerned, is our alignment with African culture, creativity, and the people shaping the continent’s stories. “For where our treasure is, our heart will be”. And this time around, our heart is in Cotonou! Oh, and so are we! Hey BNers! Osas Okonyon here, and I’m heading to the Republic of Benin for the third edition of the Salon des Industries Musicales d’Afrique Francophone (SIMA), where I’ll be over the next few days. SIMA is bringing together artists, music executives, producers, creatives, investors and other key players in the African music industry for conversations about the future of our sound, the business behind it, and how African music can continue to make its mark on the world. This year’s theme, “African Music: From the Stage to Global Influence,” is particularly exciting. Beyond the music we love and the artists we celebrate, there’s so much to explore about the business, opportunities, collaborations and structures that help African creativity thrive. From conversations around music financing, artificial intelligence and intellectual property to the intersections of music, fashion, film, tourism and sports, SIMA promises a fascinating look into the evolving creative landscape. So, whether you’re a music lover, a creative, an industry enthusiast or simply someone who loves experiencing Africa through its people and culture, come along with me. I’ll be bringing you the conversations, the discoveries, the behind-the-scenes moments and, of course, all the good vibes from Cotonou. Put on your seatbelts, BNers. We’re about to get into the sound and influence of African music! item.title: What time will SpaceX launch Starship Flight 15, its 1st double landing test, today? (Full mission timeline)
item.description:
Tariq is the Editor-in-Chief of Space.com based out of our New York City office and joined the team in 2001, first as an intern and staff writer, and later as an editor. He covers human spaceflight, exploration and space science, as well as skywatching and entertainment. He became Space.com's Managing Editor in 2009 and Editor-in-Chief in 2019. In October 2022, Tariq received the Harry Kolcum Award for excellence in space reporting from the National Space Club Florida Committee. In June 2025, the National Space Society awarded him the Space Pioneer Award for Excellence in Mass Media at the International Space Development Conference in Orlando, Florida.

Hailing from Stockton, California (where he attended the same high school as NASA astronaut Jose Hernandez), Tariq studied print journalism and astronomy at the University of Southern California in Los Angeles, earning a bachelor's degree in journalism in 1999 along with a minor in astronomy. He then served as a staff reporter for The Los Angeles Times covering education and city beats in La Habra and Fullerton in Orange County for the Our Times sections.

In 2000, Tariq became the city reporter for the Huntington Beach Independent, a weekly publication of the Los Angeles Times, covering local politics and events, crime, business and environmental issues. He left the Los Angeles Times in 2001 to study science journalism at New York University, where he earned a master's degree in 2002 from NYU's Science and Environmental Reporting Program (now the Science, Health and Environmental Reporting Program) under the direction of space reporter William Burrows.

Tariq first joined Space.com as an intern in September 2001 while also serving as a research assistant for nutrition writer Gary Taubes and writing freelance projects, where his work appeared in The Scientist and Laboratory Equipment Magazine. He became a full-time reporter covering spaceflight in 2004, with this first launch being NASA's STS-114 Return to Flight mission in July 2005.

Tariq is also an Eagle Scout (yes, he has the Space Exploration merit badge) and went to Space Camp four times as a kid and a fifth time as an adult. When not writing about space, you can find Tariq watching the latest Star Trek TV series, sci-fi movies and reading about hippos, his favorite animal. You can find Tariq at Space.com and as the co-host to the This Week In Space podcast with space historian Rod Pyle on the TWiT network. To see his latest project, you can follow Tariq on Twitter @tariqjmalik.

item.title: Forget the Usual Black Suit, Priscilla Ojo Is Making a Case for Chocolate Brown
item.description: Priscilla Ojo wearing an embellished chocolate brown suit co-ord paired with pointed-toe camel pumps Who says a business launch calls for the usual power suit? Priscilla Ojo had a different idea when she stepped out to introduce her latest venture, PalmPriy. The content creator, entrepreneur and style tastemaker chose a rich chocolate brown two-piece, but this was no ordinary office suit. With bronze and amber beaded fringe running across the jacket, her look brought a little extra personality to corporate dressing. The suit makes a case for giving brown tailoring a place in your wardrobe. Its single-breasted blazer features sharp shoulders and a defined waist, while the floor-length wide-leg trousers give the outfit a relaxed, fluid finish. Then come the embellishments: heavy bronze and amber beads tracing the lapels, hemline and cuffs. They add movement and texture to the jacket, making it the piece that draws the eye without overwhelming the overall look. Priscilla Ojo styled in a custom beaded chocolate brown suit for the official launch of her business, PalmPriy. Priscilla also got the proportions right with her footwear. She paired the wide-leg trousers with pointed-toe camel pumps, allowing just a glimpse of the shoes beneath the long hems. The rest of her accessories stayed simple, with subtle drop earrings and delicate rings leaving the embellished suit plenty of room to speak for itself. A detailed view of Priscilla Ojo’s chocolate brown blazer featuring hand-sewn pearls and beaded fringe. Her beauty look followed the warm colour palette. She wore her hair in long, cascading waves with copper highlights, parted down the middle, and completed the look with bronze-toned soft glam and a glossy nude lip. For anyone looking to take their tailoring beyond the familiar black or grey suit, Priscilla’s PalmPriy launch outfit offers a lovely starting point. Chocolate brown, wide-leg trousers and a little embellishment make for a combination worth considering, whether you’re dressing for a business event or looking to give your workwear a new direction. item.description: null SpaceX is one big step closer to the 15th test flight of its Starship megarocket. The company announced today (Nov. 10) that it had moved its latest Starship first stage, known as Super Heavy Booster 22, to the launch mount at its Starbase facility in South Texas ahead of Flight 15, which is scheduled to lift off this Friday (Nov. 13). During the upcoming launch test, SpaceX plans to catch both Booster 22 and Starship's Ship upper stage with its launch tower's "chopstick" arms in a double landing catch — something the private spaceflight company has never tried before. It will be the first full recovery of an orbital rocket in history. SpaceX's Flight 15 Starship Super Heavy booster in its assembly bay, before its move to Starbase's launch mount. (Image credit: SpaceX) Booster 22 therefore "was used for final catch testing upon arrival [at the pad], including a suspended squeeze test at catch height," SpaceX said in an X post today (Nov. 10). That post shared four photos of the giant booster, which is powered by 33 of SpaceX's next-gen Raptor engines. The first shot showed Super Heavy in one of Starbase's "Mega Bay" assembly buildings before rollout, while the other three depicted it grasped by the tower's arms, held high in the South Texas sky. SpaceX will try to catch both Super Heavy and Ship during Flight 15 — something it's never done before. (Image credit: SpaceX) SpaceX has used the chopstick arms during Starship flights before; it has successfully caught Super Heavy on three separate occasions. But the company has never attempted a catch of Ship, which flies higher and farther than the booster and is therefore a more challenging target. And SpaceX only reached orbit with Starship for the first time on Flight 14, which launched on Sept. 28. So Flight 15 will break new ground. And, if all goes to plan, it will give us a look at the future: SpaceX plans to catch Super Heavy and Ship on all operational Starship missions, as this recovery strategy will allow the company to boost the megarocket's launch cadence. And SpaceX wants to fly Starship incredibly often, so that it can build out its Starlink V3 broadband constellation and even bigger Starmind AI data-center network . Indeed, Elon Musk has said the company is eyeing 10,000 Starship flights per year by 2030. The launch tower's "chopstick" arms giving the Flight 15 Super Heavy a loving squeeze. (Image credit: SpaceX) If all goes to plan, Flight 15 will launch from Starbase on Friday during a 75-minute window that opens at 5:45 p.m. EST (2245 GMT; 4:45 p.m. local Texas time). Super Heavy will return to Starbase for its catch about 6.5 minutes after liftoff. Ship will follow suit much later — about 22 hours later, in fact, after it has deployed 26 Starlink V3 spacecraft into LEO and completed 14 circuits of our planet. You can watch all the action live here at Space.com and get updates about the mission here .

item.title: Anthony Mackie, Ariana DeBose, and John Leguizamo reveal why they joined Andy Weir's sci-fi audio drama 'Exoplanet' (interview)
item.description: null In any respectable audiobook project, finding the names of Andy Weir ("The Martian," "Project Hail Mary") and Benjamin Percy ("The Ninth Metal," "Wolverine") attached would elicit intense fan interest, but add the superstar vocal talents of Anthony Mackie ("Avengers: Infinity War," "Avengers: Doomsday"), Ariana DeBose ("West Side Story"), and John Leguizamo ("Ice Age"), and it catapults this sonic odyssey into the stratosphere. Such is the case with " Exoplanet ," Audible Original’s new 7-episode science fiction audio drama executive produced by Weir and penned by Percy. Its planet-hopping space disaster narrative sees the crew of the starship Wild Blue Yonder hit a quantum anomaly, forcing their ship to crash-land onto a deadly exoplanet. All is not as it seems, though, as each crew member arrives in a different era on the same world. We hooked up with Mackie, DeBose, and Lequizamo to learn more about this renaissance of audio dramas and what attracted them to board Weir's sci-fi thriller. One crew. One planet. Three timelines. No one survives alone. A sci-fi thriller executive produced by Andy Weir (#1 bestselling author of Project Hail Mary , The Martian ), with an all-star cast led by Anthony Mackie, Ariana DeBose and John Leguizamo. Exoplanet is free for Audible members, but also available for purchase separately. View Deal Mackie voices Chief Engineer Jeff Shaw. His attraction to the imaginative genre began at an early age thanks to some cool family friends while growing up in the Big Easy. "My brother went to college at Morehouse," he tells SPACE. "I was like 8, and he was 18. He’d always bring friends home, because New Orleans is a party city, so they'd come over and get drunk. But one of his friends gave me a book by Walter Mosley and one by Octavia Butler, and I got hooked into sci-fi and the future." "From 'Back to the Future' to 'Aliens,' the future was such an idea of what was going to be out there. Now we’re living it," reveals Mackie. "It’s very important to me as a human being to have that construct as a part of my career. The only thing more arrogant than wanting to be president is standing up and saying, 'Yeah, I can go to space.' That sounds crazy to me." "Exoplanet" was released by Audible on Nov. 5, 2026. (Image credit: Audible) Leguizamo's New York City childhood was influenced by absorbing classic radio dramas of the past, which primed him for this special Audible project. “It was Anthony and Ariana being in it that really pumped me up, and of course Andy Weir," he recalls regarding his portrayal of Science Officer Logan Bowers. "Then when I got the theme, that it was something relevant today and makes you think about computers and technology taking over and making us obsolete. It just hit me in that right zeitgeist, at that right little point." "As a poor kid, there was no YouTube or cell phones, and we didn’t have computers," reminisces Leguizamo. item.title: On this day in space! Nov. 10, 2013: Europe's GOCE satellite, the 'Ferrari of space,' fell out of orbit after mapping Earth's gravity field
item.description: null On Nov. 10, 2013, Europe's GOCE satellite fell to Earth after four years in orbit mapping the planet's gravitational field. GOCE, its name was short for Gravity field and steady-state Ocean Circulation Explorer, launched in 2009 on a mission to map Earth's gravity like never before. But despite that successful mission, it was doomed in 2013 when it ran out of fuel . At the time, controllers weren't sure where GOCE would fall back to Earth . Some people worried that it might crash into a populated area. However, the small spacecraft broke up in the atmosphere and didn't cause any property damage. It disintegrated about 50 miles above the Falkland Islands in the South Atlantic Ocean. The European Space Agency called the mission a success. GOCE lasted far longer than expected. It showed small variations in Earth's gravity , mapped the structure of Earth's crust and mantle, and tracked ocean currents. Artist's rendering of the "Ferrari of space," the European Space Agency's Gravity field and steady-state Ocean Circulation Explorer (GOCE), before it fell from space in 2013. (Image credit: European Space Agency) Why it mattered The GOCE satellite was a sleek spacecraft, with fins covered in solar panels that gave it a futuristic design. In fact, its look earned it a pretty cool nickname. "GOCE's sleek, elegant aerodynamic design — responsible for it being dubbed the 'Ferrari of space' — immediately set it apart from most other satellites,." ESA officials said in a description . There was more than looks behind GOCE's design. In order to generate the best map ever of Earth's gravitational field, GOCE had to fly in an orbit so low — just 139 miles (224 kilometers) — it needed to counteract the drag from the gossamer thin atmosphere of Earth at that altitude. The International Space Station orbits Earth at nearly twice that altitude. GOCE was powered by an xenon ion engine that allowed to maintain its low orbit for four years. Once it ran out of fuel, the 1-ton satellite could not maintain its position in space , leading to a fiery plunge to Earth. The large size of GOCE — it weighed 2,425 pounds (1,100 kilograms) and was 17 feet (5.3 meters) long and 3.2 feet (1 m) wide — made its reentry stand out, particularly since at least 25% of the satellite was expected to reach the Earth's surface . Want more space history? Check out our full On This Day In Space Story archive and watch our On This Day In Space videos on YouTube .

item.title: A distant exoplanet mysteriously vanished from sight. Astronomers just discovered why
item.description: null Astronomers have solved the mystery of an extrasolar planet, or exoplanet, that "disappeared" after seven years of observations. New research suggests that the planet hasn't vanished at all, but has been dragged off its orbit by an unseen planet. The exoplanet , designated TOI-2535 b, is located around 1,000 light-years away. TOI-2535 b was routinely observed with NASA's Transiting Exoplanet Survey Satellite ( TESS ) space telescope for seven years between April 2019 and March 2026 as it completed its 8.25-Earth day orbit of its parent star. That's 10 times quicker than the orbit of Mercury around the sun and means this blisteringly hot planet is classed as a " hot Jupiter ." However, something strange happened started to happen as astronomers observed the distant world. The orbits of the planet weren't regular like those of other planets, with TOI-2535 b often arriving six hours early or six hours later than when astronomers expected. Then, in March this year, TESS was no longer spotting the characteristic drops in starlight that TOI-2535 b caused as it crossed, or "transited," the face of its parent star. It seemed to have vanished. This team used TESS data to determine that TOI-2535 b is being pulled on by an unseen neighbor and is, in turn, pulling on that planet as well. This is causing the orbits of both worlds in the TOI-2535 system to "wobble." TOI-2535 b disappeared when that wobble tilted it out of alignment with its star. "We think of the universe as resembling clockwork, where everything is regular, but that's not true. If there are multiple planets in a system, they can affect each other's orbits. We know of a few systems that are like this," team member Samuel Yee of the University of California, Los Angeles, said in a statement . "This is the most extreme example we've seen because the two planets are interacting so strongly. The planet's orbit is tilting so quickly that its transit disappeared while we were watching." TOI-2535 b isn't expected to transit its parent star for at least 30 years, but the hidden neighbor tugging on it may cross the face of the star sooner than that. In the meantime, scientists will attempt to decode what this extreme wobbling exoplanet system says about how it formed. Hot Jupiters should be cool customers There is currently a lot of speculation about how hot Jupiter planets like TOI-2535 b form. That is because current routes of planet formation suggest planets like this would need to form around a great deal of ice. Obviously, ice isn't likely to be abundant as close to a star as TOI-2535 b is currently. This means that hot Jupiters likely form far from their stars and then migrate inwards . There are two ways that this could happen. The planet could be excited into an elliptical orbit by violent events like a near-collision with another planetary object, and then interactions with the star pull the planet inwards. Alternatively, the hot Jupiter may be pulled inwards along with the other planets

Passport Legacy Hosts Business Leaders, Partners with CEO IMA Grenada to Drive Strategic Global Mobility Solutions
item.description: Passport Legacy under the division of the Passport Legacy Group is a leading firm that specializes in global citizenship, residency, international real estate, and corporate solutions like company setup, hosted an intimate cocktail evening featuring Special Guest Thomas Anthony , CEO of IMA Grenada. The event gathered founders, executives, and everyday professionals to explore generational wealth protection, strategic investments, and second citizenship opportunities. The evening commenced with a welcome address delivered by Weyinmi Oritsejiafor , Managing Director of Passport Legacy Nigeria setting the tone for the night and reaffirming the firm’s commitment to providing tailored advisory services to forward-thinking individuals. “At Passport Legacy, We are a Swiss owned advisory. We do much more than Passports. We do investment migration and government advisory” Oritsejiafor said, emphasizing that when global mobility is crucial for families and businesses to safeguard their wealth, protect their assets against volatility, and scale internationally, investment migration is a secure foundation for long-term growth. Oritsejiafor also highlighted that the Passport Legacy Group offers access to international real estate opportunities across key hubs such as Cyprus, Greece, Thailand, Bali, and Dubai. Beyond private advisory, she noted that the firm delivers government advisory services through specialized programs and framework tools, citing their engagement with the government of São Tomé and Príncipe as a key example of this institutional work. The centerpiece of the evening was a keynote presentation by Special Guest Thomas Anthony, CEO of the Investment Migration Agency Grenada (IMA Grenada). Anthony shared key insights into Grenada’s premier Citizenship by Investment (CBI) framework, detailing its unique economic advantages, tax efficiencies, and strategic global access for business owners and proactive individuals. Anthony highlighted that Grenada’s Investment Migration framework delivers a transparent gateway for global flexibility and security. Unlike direct US programs like the EB-5, which expose global income and assets to US taxation, Grenada’s E-2 visa pathway allows investors to establish business operations in the US without subjecting their offshore wealth to worldwide taxes. Anthony further explained that while Grenada itself is an intimate market, the membership in the Organisation of Eastern Caribbean States (OECS) expands direct business reach across an integrated regional market of over 700,000 people. Through a partnership with Passport Legacy, the firm provides tailored guidance to unlock international business opportunities and position Grenada as a premier destination for discerning global investors , giving Nigerian founders a dual advantage of sovereign asset protection and unhindered global growth. item.title: Nigeria’s Danielle Adewusi Begins Her Miss Universe 2026 Journey in Puerto Rico
item.description: Danielle Adewusi in a custom off-white and burgundy ensemble featuring gold embroidery and a dramatic train for her Miss Universe departure. Photo Credit: Danielle Adewusi/Instagram The road to the 75th Miss Universe crown is officially underway, and Nigeria’s representative, Dr Danielle Adewusi , has touched down in San Juan, Puerto Rico, to begin pre-pageant activities. Danielle was crowned Miss Universe Nigeria 2026 on 27 September at the Balmoral Hall, Federal Palace Hotel in Lagos. Competing as Miss Lagos State against 19 other delegates, her victory marked a full-circle moment: her mother won the national title in 1991, 35 years before her. An alumnus of King’s College London, Danielle holds an MBBS alongside a first-class honours degree in Psychology. Alongside her medical career, she leads Scrub the Stigma, an initiative focused on expanding healthcare access and raising awareness around women’s health across Nigeria and the UK. Miss Universe Nigeria 2026 Danielle Adewusi wearing her official national crown and gold sequin gown. Photo Credit: Danielle Adewusi/Instagram Before taking the national crown, she placed in the Top 5 at Miss Universe Great Britain in 2023 and completed international runway coaching in Thailand. With recent updates by the Miss Universe Organisation removing maximum age limits, 29-year-old Danielle is also among the delegates competing under the expanded eligibility rules. Arriving in San Juan on Monday, 9 November, Danielle joins nearly 120 delegates from across the globe for preliminary rounds, national costume presentations, and rehearsals. The grand finale of the 75th Miss Universe pageant takes place on Tuesday, 24 November 2026, at the Coliseo de Puerto Rico José Miguel Agrelot in San Juan. Danielle Adewusi waves the Nigerian flag at the airport as she departs for the Miss Universe 2026 pageant in Puerto Rico. item.description: Afthonia is set to host another edition of its Sample Sale on Saturday, November 14, 2026, from 10 a.m. to 7 p.m. at Alliance Française, Ikoyi, Lagos. The event will bring together Nigerian fashion brands offering selected pieces from previous collections, samples, and overstock. The event will feature 11 vendors, comprising nine clothing designers, one bag designer, and one jewellery vendor. Shoppers will have the opportunity to discover pieces from Nigerian brands while giving existing stock another chance to find buyers. At its May 2026 edition, the Afthonia Sample Sale recorded 133 pieces sold. The November edition builds on this by creating another opportunity for designers to sell existing stock that may otherwise remain in storage after newer collections are introduced. The idea behind the Sample Sale is simple: clothing that has already been made should have the opportunity to find buyers and be worn. By bringing these pieces to shoppers, Afthonia hopes to help designers make better use of existing stock while giving customers the opportunity to shop from Nigerian brands. Garment Care will also be available at the event, offering alteration services for shoppers who need adjustments to their purchases. The Afthonia Sample Sale will take place on Saturday, November 14, 2026, from 10 a.m. to 7 p.m. at Alliance Française, Ikoyi, Lagos. item.title: How Heineken Created Immersive Experiences That Took Lagos Fashion Week 2026 Beyond the Runway
item.description: In a city where creativity is a culture and every corner has a story to tell, Heineken brought another expression of Lagos to life at Lagos Fashion Week 2026 . Through its City of Cities: Where Taste Rules experience, the brand transformed its eleven-year partnership with the fashion showcase into a celebration of the people, ideas, and experiences shaping the city’s creative identity, bringing fashion, music, innovation, and social connections together across the week. From runway presentations to the Heineken Lounge, the debut of Heineken Studio, and an energetic after-party, the brand created experiences that went beyond the collections on display, inviting guests to explore new expressions of taste, discover creative possibilities, and connect over shared interests. At the heart of the experience was City of Cities: Where Taste Rules, an experience inspired by the many influences that make Lagos what it is. First introduced in 2025, the concept recognises that Lagos is more than one city; it is a melting pot of different cultures, communities, sounds, and styles. At Lagos Fashion Week 2026, Heineken brought this idea into focus, celebrating the diversity of expression that makes the city’s creative scene distinct. The experience also marked another chapter in Heineken’s eleven-year journey with Lagos Fashion Week. Over the years, the partnership has explored the intersection of fashion, craftsmanship, and taste through initiatives such as Woven Threads in 2022, the Dyelab collaboration in 2023, and the H45 Collection in 2024, before introducing City of Cities: Where Taste Rules in 2025. Each edition has created a new way to engage with fashion and culture, with this year’s experience building on that foundation through fresh expressions of creativity and innovation. Aligned with the 2026 theme, CRAFTED: Heritage. Innovation. Circular Futures, Heineken’s presence celebrated the artistry, intentionality, and evolving perspectives shaping contemporary fashion. Across the venue, guests arrived in style, adding their own interpretations of fashion and self-expression to the atmosphere. The Heineken Lounge provided a space to unwind, exchange ideas, and connect as guests enjoyed chilled Heineken, refreshments, and the runway presentations. The experience also offered a taste of something different, with guests exploring Foam Infusions in exciting variations, including espresso and blood orange. A major highlight was the Nigerian debut of Heineken Studio, the brand’s Playground of Innovation, which brought together taste, creativity, and personal expression in an interactive space. Beyond discovering new ways to experience lager through Foam Infusions, guests could step into the painting studio to create personalised designs on their own Heineken cans. The photo area and Heineken-branded backdrops also became popular spots for guests to capture their moments, express their individual styles, and share their experiences. item.title: Double Honours at Oxford! Ogechukwu Elumelu Earns Her MSc & Completes Law Conversion | See Photos
item.description: Oge Elumelu shares a high five with her father, Tony Elumelu, during her Oxford graduation celebrations. It is a double celebration in the Elumelu household. Ogechukwu Elumelu has officially added another prestigious academic feather to her cap, graduating with a Master of Science degree from the University of Oxford alongside the completion of a rigorous law conversion course. As the eldest daughter of renowned Nigerian billionaire businessman, philanthropist, and Heirs Holdings chairman Tony Elumelu and medical doctor and entrepreneur Dr Awele Elumelu , Oge has consistently charted an impressive path in academia and leadership. Oge Elumelu celebrates her Master of Science graduation beneath Oxford’s historic Bridge of Sighs. Before her recent postgraduate milestone at Oxford, she earned her undergraduate degree with honours in Politics and Philosophy from the London School of Economics and Political Science (LSE). Beyond the classroom, she is widely recognised as a dynamic young voice, hosting the podcast Africa & Everywhere: Conversations with Oge, where she interviews prominent business leaders and changemakers, and founding the Africa & Everywhere Festival in Lagos to connect young professionals with career opportunities. She is also a future trainee solicitor at White & Case LLP. The graduation ceremony in Oxford drew close family support, with both Tony Elumelu and Awele Elumelu present to cheer her on. Stepping out for the milestone event, Tony Elumelu kept it sharp and classic in a tailored dark suit paired with a crisp white shirt and tie, matching the historic academic atmosphere of the university town. Dr Awele Elumelu, Oge Elumelu, and Tony Elumelu walking together through Oxford on graduation day. Taking to social media to share his excitement, Tony Elumelu posted highlights from the celebration, writing, “Oxford MSc Graduation and Law Conversion Completed! Two major milestones. One incredible TOEGirl! Congratulations, Oge.So proud of you!” Oge Elumelu captures a graduation selfie with her parents, Dr Awele Elumelu and Tony Elumelu. item.title: 5 New Albums to Listen to This Week: Skepta, Phyno, Ty Bello & More
item.description: Skepta holding the official clear vinyl edition of his sixth studio album, The Fork and Knife. Photo Credit: Skepta/Instagram Your playlist could do with a little shake-up, and these five albums might be exactly what it needs. Skepta is reconnecting with his roots, Phyno is giving us more of the indigenous rap we love, Ty Bello has two albums exploring different expressions of worship, and Anendlessocean and Tobe Nwigwe are taking their sounds in interesting directions. From UK grime and Nigerian hip-hop to alternative gospel and soul, there’s a lot to discover across these new releases. Whether you’re in the mood for bars, worship, thoughtful songwriting or music that brings different cultures together, this week’s selection has something worth hearing. Skepta: The Fork & Knife Back in 2012, Skepta found himself at odds with a corporatised grime scene, sparking a pivotal career reckoning that eventually led to his landmark 2016 album Konnichiwa. On his long-awaited 15-track sixth album, The Fork & Knife, the 44-year-old MC reflects on his journey as grime’s most influential elder statesman and the son of Nigerian immigrants. Named after his mother’s favourite proverb, the record is a deep exploration of identity and perseverance. Musically, Skepta bridges continents by blending global diasporic sounds. He teams up with Aya Nakamura on the zouk-infused “ Chippie ”, taps Asake for the Afrobeats crossover “ Aloe Vera ”, and recruits Chase & Status alongside Suggs for the sharp single “ Innocent Smile ”. The project closes with “ Belly ”, an eight-minute masterclass featuring Boy Better Know members Jme and Frisco . ﻿ Phyno: Let That Sink In Arriving nearly 10 years after his groundbreaking sophomore record The Playmaker, Phyno’s 15-track sixth solo album, Let That Sink In (LTSI), showcases his timeless command of indigenous rap. Across the record,the Enugu-born star blends soul, R&B, and traditional Nigerian sounds to explore faith, resilience, and personal evolution. The album features powerhouse collaborations, including Seyi Vibez on the opener “ Ndu Ka Aku ”, Fireboy DML on “ I Believe ”, and Jeriq on “ Ije Enu ”. Whether taking the government to task on “20 Years to Come” or offering uplifting anthems like “ Chukwu Okike ”, Phyno proves why he remains a definitive voice in African hip-hop. ﻿ Ty Bello: I Speak Lion and I Speak Lamb Creative powerhouse Ty Bello delivers a massive double-album listening experience with I Speak Lion and I Speak Lamb . Split into two distinct spiritual volumes, the expansive project captures both the bold, triumphant authority of worship and its quiet, intimate moments. ﻿ I Speak Lion leans into explosive, high-energy sounds designed to spark courage, featuring powerful pairings with Sunmisola Agbebi , Greatman Takit , and Limoblaze . In contrast, I Speak Lamb steps into soaking acoustic textures and tender devotional spaces, offering a complete, multi-layered sanctuary for listeners. ﻿ Anendlessocean: Freedom Alte

item.title: Ifeyinwa Azubike Reconsiders the Rules of Dressing with The Ladymaker’s Stand On Ceremony
item.description: During Lagos Fashion Week, The Ladymaker ’s Founder and Creative Director, Ifeyinwa Azubike, introduced Stand On Ceremony, a collection that considers the relationship between personal expression and the expectations attached to an occasion. Presented on 27 October 2026 at The Sphere, Lagos, the collection draws from the familiar expression to stand on ceremony: to insist on the observance of formalities. For Ifeyinwa Azubike, the idea presents an opportunity to examine the traditions women inherit, the rituals they observe and the choices they make when dressing for themselves. The collection is built around two identities: The Devotee and The Rebel. They are not opposing personalities so much as two ways of relating to ceremony. The Devotee embraces its rituals. She understands the language of formal dressing and participates in it with intention. For her, dressing fully is an expression of desire and personal conviction. The Rebel is equally familiar with the rules, but she is selective about the ones she follows. Her approach to dressing allows for disruption, though never simply for the sake of attention. Through these characters, Azubike considers a familiar experience for women: the pull between what an occasion expects and what an individual wants to express. Every woman who has dressed for an occasion has encountered this tension in some form, whether in choosing to honour a tradition or finding room to express herself within it. The garments give form to this conversation. The Cloister Dress is paired with the Banner Dress, while the Manor Jumpsuit is placed alongside the Assembly Set. Other looks, including the Herald Dress, Emissary Set, Procession Dress and Sovereign Set, extend the collection’s exploration of the two identities. Material choices move between crimson jacquard, rose jacquard, ice jacquard, denim Akwete, wine Adire, midnight sequins and beaded velvet. The collection draws on fabrics and textures that allow ceremony to be interpreted through different moods, silhouettes and degrees of formality. Stand On Ceremony was presented during Lagos Fashion Week through an intimate fashion presentation, followed by a soirée where guests could experience the garments more closely. The evening was held in partnership with MAC Cosmetics, which provided beauty; Moët & Chandon, the champagne partner; Jacque Scents, which created the fragrance experience; and The Nail Boutique , responsible for nail artistry. For Ifeyinwa Azubike, the question the collection leaves with its audience is a personal one: are you a Rebel or a Devotee? The Ladymaker Brand Profile Founded in 2015 by Ifeyinwa Azubike, The Ladymaker is a Lagos-based womenswear brand that brings together African heritage, classical elegance and contemporary design. Established by Azubike following a career in commercial law, the brand was born from a desire to create timeless clothing rooted in craftsmanship, fit and enduring style rather than fleeting trends. item.title: Leo Stan Ekeh Tells Women Leaders at TIWLC, Dubai: I Chose ‘Corporate Suicide’ Over the Safe Path
item.description: Africa’s tech icon and Chairman of Zinox Group , Leo Stan Ekeh , has told an international gathering of women leaders that his decision to build a technology company in Africa, at a time when the sector was virtually non-existent on the continent, amounted to what he described as “corporate suicide”. Speaking on the theme “Losing the Fear” , at The International Women Leadership Conference (TIWLC) in Dubai, organised by the Ibukun Awosika Leadership Foundation, Ekeh , who was a keynote speaker on the final day of this year’s conference, addressed over 600 women industry leaders from different countries across the globe. He said he returned from his studies abroad to a Nigeria where his peers were filing into banking, oil and gas, and where technology was largely seen as a foreign game. Ekeh, who studied Economics in India, said he was discouraged from pursuing a postgraduate degree in Computer Science in Europe because of the prevailing perception then that Africa might have little need for computers over the next 35 years, potentially leaving him frustrated. He subsequently opted for a postgraduate degree in Risk Management before pursuing a Master’s degree in Business Law (LLM) at London Guildhall University. He recalled that he could not sit his final law examinations because he had diverted his tuition fees into his passion for technology entrepreneurship. He also disclosed that he had fended off recruitment attempts by international technology companies that had sought to hire him before his return to Africa. “I chose the road not taken,” he told the conference. “It was corporate suicide in the eyes of my parents and many others. I lost the fear because I believed technology was the master key that would unlock possibilities for Nigeria and Africa.” He said the journey came with considerable hardship, including living on one meal a day for over three years and sleeping in a very small room in his office. According to him, his vision was to create a Nigerian and, by extension, an African IT identity. Recalling the launch of his first company, Task Systems Ltd, over 35 years ago, the company that pioneered desktop publishing and computer graphics in Nigeria. At the launch, held at the Sheraton Hotel, Ikeja, Ekeh recalled addressing an overcrowded hall filled with industry leaders, some of whom were seeing computers for the first time. He told them: “No country can claim to be independent without technology independence.” He said the Nigerian media embraced the vision, describing him as a “miracle child” and supporting the company’s roadmap. This, he noted, contributed to the computerisation of over 97 per cent of media and multimedia houses in Nigeria, as well as in other African countries. He further explained that the decision to establish Zinox Technologies, which became one of Africa’s first Microsoft WHQL- and Intel-certified computer manufacturers, was driven by the need to give Nigeria and Africa a global technology identity. “We were n

item.title: Midea Introduces Space Master Refrigerator in Nigeria, Bringing More Room to Everyday Living
item.description: Midea is introducing the Space Master Refrigerator to Nigerian consumers, placing practical food storage at the centre of its “More Room for Nigeria” campaign. The introduction speaks to a familiar household situation: a major grocery shop, a weekend of hosting or a family celebration can quickly turn refrigerator space into a daily planning challenge. Space Master is presented with a simple proposition: “Same Size. More Space. More Capacity.” Its approach to storage design gives households more usable interior space for the food, drinks and everyday essentials they need to keep at home. For households planning meals ahead, the practical question is not only what to buy, but where everything will go. Fresh produce, bottled drinks, ingredients for family meals and food prepared for guests all compete for space. Space Master’s bigger-capacity proposition gives consumers more room to accommodate larger grocery shops, everyday essentials and food for family occasions, helping households prepare more comfortably for both daily routines and celebrations. “ More Room for Nigeria” connects that functional product story to everyday Nigerian life. From stocking up for a busy working week to preparing for a family gathering, the campaign shows why usable storage matters at moments when households need flexibility. Its companion message, “Every Celebration Needs More Room,” gives the product a role in the preparations for the occasion — before guests arrive, meals are served and memories are made. The campaign also places product discovery at the heart of the consumer experience. Through planned retail demonstrations, shoppers will be invited to open the Space Master, explore its interior layout and see examples of how groceries and meal-preparation items can be arranged. The “Grocery Fit Challenge” and household grocery scenarios are designed to make the storage proposition tangible, while store representatives can answer model-specific questions and explain the purchase process. Midea ’s approach reflects a focus on applying product design and practical technology to everyday consumer needs. By making storage easier to visualize and explore, the brand aims to help shoppers evaluate how a refrigerator can suit their routines, household size and entertaining needs. Consumers interested in Space Master can enquire at authorized Midea retail outlets and request an in-store demonstration and confirmation of the specific model’s specifications, current stock availability and applicable purchase terms before making a decision. Executive Comment “In many homes, food storage becomes especially important when everyday routines meet the demands of hosting and celebration. With Space Master, we want consumers to experience how thoughtful refrigerator design can help them organize the things that matter to their households. ‘More Room for Nigeria’ brings that practical idea to life,” said Louis Zang, Home Appliances Sales Manager for Midea Nigeria. item.description: Funke Akindele in a custom off-white Eki Kere buba and iro styled by Zack Styling. Funke Akindele has a new Yoruba-inspired look on our fashion radar, and this one comes with plenty of details to admire. For the London premiere announcement of her upcoming film, The Four , the Nollywood star stepped out in a custom Eki Kere buba and iro, giving the traditional two-piece a fresh interpretation with oversized floral appliqués and a striking colour combination. Styled by Zack Styling, the off-white buba features wide sleeves decorated with bold crimson rosettes that extend across the shoulders. Its matching iro midi skirt takes a different floral route, with bright yellow-and-red sunflower motifs arranged from the waist to the hem. The matching headscarf, finished with floral detailing, completes the traditional look,while a chunky multi-layered beaded necklace and drop earrings add more texture around the neckline. For footwear,Funke chose crimson ankle-strap platform sandals, bringing another hit of colour to the outfit. Detailing on Funke Akindele’s multi-layered beaded necklace, matching headscarf, and Eki Kere buba top. The look is a lovely showcase of how traditional Yoruba dressing can accommodate a more expressive approach to colour, embellishment and styling. The Eki Kere buba and iro already have a distinct silhouette, but the floral detailing gives Funke’s custom set its own identity without taking away from the traditional design. There’s also a major film announcement behind the appearance. The Four , is heading to London for its grand premiere on Sunday, 29 November 2026, at ODEON Luxe Leicester Square. The film is scheduled to open in Nigerian cinemas nationwide on 11 December 2026. From psychological drama and riverine mysteries to corporate battles and family betrayals, here are five films bringing different stories to the screen. 7 Years Silence (Bolaji Ogunmola TV) What happens when a web of long-kept secrets finally unravels after nearly a decade? 7 Years Silence follows a devoted wife who, after seven years of marriage and a painful struggle to conceive, discovers her seemingly perfect husband has been living a complete double life. As hidden motives and suppressed truths explode into the open, every character is forced to face the shattering fallout of a marriage built on an illusion. Newly engaged Morayo and Akindele travel to his hometown to celebrate their future, but beside a forbidden river, Morayo’s recurring nightmares begin to unearth a devastating truth. item.title: Nkanyeziyethu Malunga: The Zimbabwean Designer Preserving African Heritage Through Fashion
item.description: At her workshop in Bulawayo, Zimbabwe, Nkanyeziyethu Malunga crafted colour into fabric, using plants, tree bark and other natural materials gathered from the environment. Choosing a colour or designing a pattern is only one of the processes. Each material carries details on how it was gathered, prepared, and transformed, which Malunga is incorporating into contemporary fashion. “My dyes are mainly extracted from plants such as mnyii and hibiscus. Although I also use many other plants, including tubers, that have properties suitable for dye extraction. I love hibiscus not only for its petals, which produce beautiful dyes, but also for its tea.” The 37-year-old designer is challenging conventional notions about what defines a fashion collection and where creative knowledge originates. Through her clothing business, GANU, she transforms indigenous materials and skills into clothes and accessories, demonstrating how knowledge passed down through generations can inform modern design, provide opportunities for rural women, and conserve cultural practices. Her method is based on teachings learned from her late maternal grandmother, Ngatsha Nkatha, who resided in Tsholotsho, a rural district in Zimbabwe. During the school vacations, Malunga and her siblings traveled from Bulawayo to visit grandma, witnessing as she turned sisal, sedge, and reeds into winnowing baskets. “When I was a child, I often visited my grandmother in the village with my siblings. She was very dexterous with her fingers, and that passion eventually became mutual.” Malunga started experimenting with fashion in her teens before launching Ganu in 2013. The name is derived from iganu, the Ndebele term for marula fruit, and represents her connection to local resources and African identity. Her creations blend basketry, crocheting, batik, and beadwork with natural dyes, leather, and other locally produced materials. For Malunga, the importance of these materials goes beyond their appearance. Bamboo, sisal, reeds, and sedge are used in basketry, and she breeds Angora goats for their fur, which she straightens and dyes to make garments. Cowhide obtained from local abattoirs is softened in a tannery before being mixed into leather designs. “I keep Angora goats for the fur needed in garment production. However, for raw materials such as cowhide, I usually source these from local abattoirs while sisal and tree barks are either harvested by me or sometimes extracted by colleagues I work with, who are based in the rural areas.” Desmond Ntini , a cultural entrepreneur based in Bulawayo, sees Malunga’s work as part of a broader shift in how African history is perceived and used. ” Malunga is redefining the fashion industry by blending traditional African influences with contemporary creativity. Her work explains how our cultural identity can inspire modern designs while opening doors for sustainable fashion, business opportunities, and the celebration of African heritage.” Ntini said. Too big – and too well-connected – to sack? One doesn’t have to be overly cynical to think Jensen Huang, the Nvidia boss, starts with one huge advantage as the chipmaker’s board starts its independent investigation into the alleged honeytrap spy scandal . The world of US big tech is not, to put it mildly, strong on checks and balances on a founder’s power. Huang does not enjoy the supercharged voting rights that are par for the course elsewhere – his shareholding is a plain vanilla 3.6%. On the other hand, Nvidia’s board does not appear to have spent much time worrying about succession planning and “key person risk” or other standard concerns of corporate governance wonks outside the US. item.title: Carex Rewards Consumers As Everybody Wins Promo Concludes With Grand Finale Live Draw
item.description: Carex, one of Nigeria’s leading personal hygiene brands, has successfully concluded its nationwide Everybody Wins Promo with a transparent Grand Finale Live Draw , rewarding loyal consumers and reinforcing its commitment to delivering value beyond personal care products. The campaign, which ran from June 2026 to August 2026, attracted millions of consumers PAN Nigeria and rewarded winners with prizes worth over ₦400,000,000. The Grand Finale Live Draw, held in Lagos, brought together consumers, media representatives, trade partners, regulatory officials, and other key stakeholders to witness the selection of the campaign’s grand prize winner through a transparent and independently supervised process. The event marked the culmination of months of consumer participation and engagement, further strengthening the connection between the Carex brand and its consumers. Throughout the promotion, participants had multiple opportunities to win exciting rewards, including instant Recharge Cards, shopping Vouchers, and a brand-new Car. Over 90,000 consumers emerged as winners over the course of the campaign. The grand prize car winner, Faith Stephen from Ijebu Ode, Ogun State, emerged through the live draw process conducted in accordance with all applicable promotional and regulatory requirements. Speaking at the event, Ifunanya Anwunah , Head of Category – Personal Hygiene, said: “At Carex, we believe that the consumers who trust our products every day deserve to be appreciated and rewarded. The Everybody Wins Promo was created as a tangible expression of our gratitude for the loyalty and support we continue to receive from Nigerian families. “ The overwhelming participation and enthusiasm witnessed throughout this campaign demonstrate the strong connection consumers have with the Carex brand. The promo was built on a simple promise: giving everyday consumers the opportunity to win meaningful rewards while enjoying the quality, care, and protection they have come to trust from Carex. As a brand trusted by millions of Nigerians for their personal hygiene and care needs, Carex remains committed to developing initiatives that deepen consumer engagement, reward loyalty, and create memorable experiences for consumers across the country. The successful completion of the Everybody Wins Promo further underscores the brand’s commitment to putting consumers at the heart of everything it does. About Carex Carex is committed to winning the war against germs through a range of antibacterial products that support the health, hygiene, and wellbeing of consumers. Through innovative products and engaging consumer initiatives, Carex continues to build meaningful connections with families across Nigeria, delivering trusted products that help consumers live healthier and more confident lives.
